note: Adversarial review of the netsync co-op stack, 2026-10-25, live tree at the s145 tip. Each finding was checked by 1-2 independent skeptics (reachability lens; mitigation+severity lens). verdict: CONFIRMED = every skeptic confirmed; PLAUSIBLE = split; DROPPED = refuted. Line numbers are against the shared engine tree and drift.

findings.title: Behind the bridge, encounter and autosave suppression never ends after the host quits (PEER-ALIVE law broken at the suppress site)
findings.claim: SuppressEncounters is computed from `_socket.IsConnected`, which on the relay path reads only the loopback hop to the local bridge. When the host quits, the bridge keeps that hop up indefinitely, so after the exit ramp hands the guest back its own save, the guest keeps playing with random encounters off and the autosave disabled (EventEngine's noSave includes SuppressEncounters) until it turns FollowHost off or stops the bridge.
findings.failure_scenario: A guest on the relay with FollowHost=1 is mirroring; the host quits cleanly. The relay tears down the session and closes the guest's leg (main.go:158-163). The bridge only redials the upstream (bridge.py:20, 586-593); the relay is reachable, so the hard cap never trips and the game hop stays up. If the game's 75 s ReceiveTimeout ever fires, it reconnects within 2 s, inside EncounterGraceMs. The session grace runs out and the ramp reloads the guest's own autosave, but `connected` stays true, so suppress stays true: no random battles and no autosave on any later field entry, with a 'connecting' overlay. The guest plays solo for an hour. Then either the host rejoins (mirror re-arms, a later ramp reloads the pre-session-1 autosave) or the guest quits and uses Continue. Either way every solo hour since the first ramp is lost unless they manually saved. The same applies to a guest playing while it waits for the host to come online.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:1786-1789 the comment says 'a deliberate session end simply ages out in 5s'; :1790 `Boolean connected = _socket.IsConnected;`; :1801-1802 `sessionHeld = _storyMirroring || _sessionState == SessionGrace; suppress = _followHost && (connected || withinGrace || sessionHeld);`; :1808 `NetSyncVisitor.SuppressEncounters = suppress;`. NetSyncRelay.cs:177/190 `_connected` is true for as long as the WS to 127.0.0.1 is open. EventEngine.cs:693 `noSave |= NetSyncVisitor.SuppressEncounters || ...IsMirroringStory`. SettingsState.cs:53-54 IsNoEncounter includes SuppressEncounters. netsync_bridge.py:97-102 gives up (closing the game hop) only when the upstream is unreachable for 45 s; :380 the idle reap needs both directions quiet, and the game's 30 Hz position frames keep it alive. relay main.go:140-147 and :158-163 tear down and close the leg, and the bridge just redials.
findings.fix_sketch: Key the suppression on PEER-ALIVE: track a `_lastPeerAliveTick` from `_socket.IsConnected && GetRemote().Valid`, and use `suppress = _followHost && _role == "client" && (now - _lastPeerAliveTick < EncounterGraceMs || sessionHeld)`. Drop the bare `connected` term, or keep it only for the direct-TCP transport. Once _sessionState == SessionEnded and the ramp has fired, suppression should be off.

findings.title: The ending is unfollowable: Field(16000) is always bounced on the guest, and the PreEnding UI state blocks every follow-warp through fields 3000-3012
findings.claim: RedirectGuestFieldJump has no ENDING exemption, so the guest's own Field(16000) can never match LastHostField and is bounced into a reload of the final field. Inside the ending chain the follow cannot correct anything, because both follow paths require UIState.FieldHUD and the engine sets PreEnding for fields 3000-3012.
findings.failure_scenario: A co-op pair finishes the game. On field 3011 (test2_806, Dagger_Queen_Loop), the host's Field(16000) takes it to the staff roll (nextMode 4), and its lane now reports field 0. The guest's copy reaches Field(16000): dest 16000 is neither myField 3011 nor LastHostField 0, so it bounces into a reload of 3011. The replay (Wait 180+60+25+2, about 9 s) ends in Field(16000) again. The guest replays the final beat 3 times (about 30 s of reload and white fade) before the bounce budget lets the 4th through. Earlier in the chain (3001->3000->3004->...->3011), each of the guest's own Field(next) calls passes only if the host is still standing on `next`. The guest lags because it entered via a follow or a diorama return. If the host has already moved on, the jump is bounced, and no follow-warp can rescue it (PreEnding). A bounce in field 3000, whose loop has more than 21 s of explicit waits, never fills the budget (see the bounce-budget finding), so the guest loops that ending field forever. The only escape is quitting co-op.
findings.evidence: EventEngine.DoEventCode.cs:1031-1032 calls RedirectGuestFieldJump for every MAPJUMP under SpectatorField. NetSyncClient.cs:439-440 passes only `dest == myField || dest == LastHostField`, then :441-464 bounces. There is no FLDSCRPT_EVTNO_ENDING case, though the host side excludes it at :5137 and ServiceIntentFollow at :5371. gateways.md:204-209 asked for ENDING to be special-cased, but only the intent got it. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:257-261 handles Field(16000) as nextMode 4 (the ending), and FF9Define.cs:211 defines it as 16000. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:125-138 calls ChangeUIState(PreEnding) for MapNo 3000-3012. NetSyncClient.cs:3735 (FollowHostTick) and :5388 (ServiceIntentFollow, DEFER) require State == FieldHUD. LastHostField = rs.Field (:1816), which is 0 once the host's field map is gone (:1746-1757). Stock bytes: C:/gd/FFIX/reference/test2/test2_806.txt:443 `Field( 16000 )` in Dagger_Queen_Loop after about 267 frames of waits. test2_795.txt (3000) Vivi_Loop :1045-1356 holds 635 frames of Wait plus 21 anim/walk waits before Field(3004).
findings.fix_sketch: In RedirectGuestFieldJump, pass dest == FLDSCRPT_EVTNO_ENDING untouched (the guest's own ending), and pass any jump whose source or destination is in the 3000-3012 ending band (a non-interactive chain both machines play identically). Alternatively accept UIState.PreEnding as follow-eligible in FollowHostTick and ServiceIntentFollow. Also accept `dest == the host's live intent field` (F3.2-DESIGN CLA-11) so a lagging guest's own Field(next) passes.

I traced it end to end in the live tree, and the mechanism holds at every hop. It has two halves.

(1) The Field(16000) bounce on the guest always happens. It is deterministic.
- Each ending field's script ends in a MAPJUMP. On the guest, every MAPJUMP under SpectatorField goes through RedirectGuestFieldJump.
- In gMode 1 that function passes a jump only when dest == fldMapNo or dest == LastHostField. There is no ENDING case anywhere in it.
- LastHostField is the host's lane field. That field is fldMapNo only while the host has a control character on a loaded field, and 0 otherwise.
- For nextMode 4, ff9ShutdownStateFieldMap never writes fldMapNo, so the host can never report 16000.
- Result: on 3011 the guest's Field(16000) is bounced into a reload of 3011.
- 3011 runs a global stage machine on VAR_GlobUInt8_24, and its Main_Init does not reset that counter. Each reload therefore replays only stage 5: Wait 180+60+25+2, about 9 s, then Field(16000) again.
- The bounce streak has a sliding 20 s window and a budget of 3. So the guest gets 3 forced replays, about 30 s with white fades, and the 4th jump is let through. This half delays the ending but resolves itself; it is not a softlock.

(2) Nothing can correct the guest inside the ending chain.
- The chain is 2934 -> 3001 -> 3000 -> 3004 -> 3002 -> 3007 -> 3005 -> 3006 -> 3003 -> 3008 -> 3012 -> 3009 -> 3010 -> 3011 -> 16000.
- HonoluluFieldMain sets PreEnding for 3000-3012 on the first frame. That runs after UIManager's level-load FieldHUD, and 2934 also sets PreEnding mid-scene.
- Both follow paths return unless State == FieldHUD: FollowHostTick at :3735 and ServiceIntentFollow at :5388.
- So a guest Field(next) passes only while the host is standing on `next`.

The infinite loop is real but depends on timing. 3000's Main_Init resets VAR_GlobUInt8_24 = 0, so a bounce replays the whole Vivi scene: 635 frames of explicit waits plus 26 anim/window waits, more than 21 s. Bounces that far apart never stay inside the 20

The bounce budget (MaxBounceStreak 3 inside a 20 s sliding window, NetSyncClient.cs:442-455) lets Field(16000) through on the 4th try, because 3011's stage-5 replay is about 9 s. votes.reason:
Every code-level claim holds on the live tree, and I found no guard, later patch or ratified decision covering the guest's own ending.

**Field(16000).** RedirectGuestFieldJump lets a jump through only when dest is fldMapNo or LastHostField. LastHostField comes from the host's position lane, which carries 0 or a real field id, never 16000. So the guest's Field(16000) is always bounced. 3011's loop is about 9 s (267 Wait frames, no windows), well inside the 20 s sliding window. The budget therefore produces exactly 3 reloads before the 4th call goes through. This part is deterministic on every co-op ending: the guest reaches the staff roll about 30 s late. It is a delay, not a softlock.

**No rescue inside 3000-3012.** HonoluluFieldMain sets PreEnding on the first HonoUpdate, after UIManager.OnLevelWasLoaded has set FieldHUD, so PreEnding wins. Both follow paths require FieldHUD. The manual teleport requires user control, which the ending's cutscenes hold off. The bounce budget's docstring says a let-through "self-corrects (the follow-warp yanks the guest back)". In PreEnding that is not true, so the rule is a wish, not enforced at the call site.

**The softlock is real.** Several ending fields take longer than 20 s on a replay: 3001 has about 38 s of explicit waits, 3000 about 21 s plus 10 windows, 3008 about 20 s, and 3009 about 16 s plus 15 windows. When the host is on another field, each guest window is orphaned, which adds about 5+2+2 s per page. On such a field each bounce resets the streak to 1, so the guest reloads forever. Even a bounce on a short field cascades. After the let-through the guest is several fields behind, so every later jump bounces too, until it reaches a long field and loops forever.

**Trigger likelihood (my inference, not traced end to end).** The dialogue lock closes a blocking guest window at the host's close plus network latency. That collapses the guest's lag below the host's fade and load time, so the guest's own Field(next) fires bef
votes.mitigated_by: Not mitigated in co-op. The only escape is to unfollow: the exit ramp settles by ExitRampSettleMaxMs (NetSyncClient.cs:663, :1383-1406) and autoloads the guest's own save, so nothing is lost, but the guest misses the ending. A 2934 bounce is rescued, because its reload returns to FieldHUD and the follow fires. A bounce inside 3000-3012 is not.

findings.title: Direct-LAN host: Stop() never closes the TcpListener, so a live co-op restart leaves a zombie listener and the new host cannot bind
findings.claim: NetSyncSocket.Stop() closes only the current peer socket. HostLoop's listener is a local blocked in AcceptSocket(), so after any transport reconfigure the old thread keeps the port bound while ApplyConfigChange immediately dials a new NetSyncSocket on the same port. Separately, HostLoop has no per-iteration exception handling, so any accept-path exception ends hosting for the rest of the process.
findings.failure_scenario: The host picks Workspace Co-op 'Host' + 'home network' and clicks Start with the game on a field. Before the friend joins, the host clicks Stop (disable_coop writes Enabled=0) and then Start again (coop host --lan writes Enabled=1). Both edits change tsig, so ApplyConfigChange runs: Stop() leaves the old HostLoop in AcceptSocket, and the next Update creates a new NetSyncSocket(host, 49200) whose TcpListener.Start() hits WSAEADDRINUSE. The new instance logs 'host loop failed' once and dies. When the friend dials, the zombie accepts, sees _running=false, closes the socket, exits and stops its listener, so nothing is listening any more. Every later guest dial is refused. The host's overlay still says 'waiting for the other player to connect (direct LAN...)' until the game is relaunched. Even with a guest connected the outcome is a race: Stop wakes the old reader asynchronously, and the new thread may bind before the old thread reaches listener.Stop().
findings.evidence: Stop: `_running = false; try { if (_conn != null) _conn.Close(); } catch { }` (NetSyncSocket.cs:544-548). The listener is local to HostLoop (`TcpListener listener = null; ... listener = new TcpListener(IPAddress.Any, _port); listener.Start();` :606-610). The loop blocks in `Socket s = listener.AcceptSocket();` (:614) and the listener is stopped only in the finally after the loop exits (:622). With no guest, `_conn` is null or an already-closed old socket, so nothing unblocks AcceptSocket. ApplyConfigChange: `_socket.Stop(); _socket = null;` (NetSyncClient.cs:1157-1161), called from the Update poll (:1318-1320). The same Update redials: `if (_socket == null) { ... _socket = new NetSyncSocket(_role == "host", _peer, _port); _socket.Start(); }` (:1719-1736). tsig covers enabled, role, peer, port, relay, code and insecure (:1087-1088). Triggers: coopdoc.disable_coop writes Enabled 0 (workspace/coopdoc.py:564-570); start_coop runs `coop host --lan` (coopdoc.py:500-502, coop.py:690-708). A zombie that accepts runs HandleConnection, whose ReadLoop is `while (_running && s.Connected)`, i.e. it exits at once (:672), then the loop exits and the listener stops. One-shot hosting: HostLoop's only try/catch wraps the whole while loop (:607-621), so a SocketException from AcceptSocket (WSAECONNRESET is a documented accept() error) or from `s.NoDelay` (HandleConnection's first line, outside its try, :649) ends hosting. ClientLoop, by contrast, has a per-iteration try/catch plus a 2 s retry (:627-643). The Python bridge's accept loop explicitly survives transient accept errors (netsync_bridge.py:786-795).
findings.fix_sketch: Hold the TcpListener in a field and have Stop() call listener.Stop() (this unblocks AcceptSocket with a SocketException the loop treats as exit). Put each accept + HandleConnection iteration inside its own try/catch with a short backoff, as ClientLoop does. Retry a failed bind with backoff, and surface it on the overlay ('port N in use -- relaunch or change Port') instead of dying after one log line. Optionally join the old accept thread for up to ~1 s in ApplyConfigChange before redialing the same port.

votes.reason:
I traced the path end to end in the live tree and it can be reached with real inputs through a documented UI flow. NetSyncSocket.Stop() only sets _running=false and closes _conn. A host with no guest has _conn == null, because _conn is assigned only in HandleConnection, so nothing wakes HostLoop's local TcpListener. That listener stays blocked in AcceptSocket and keeps the port bound.

The Workspace "Turn co-op off" button (disable_coop) writes Enabled=0. "Start" then runs `coop host --lan`, which writes Enabled=1 and RelayUrl="". The CLI also documents off followed by `coop host` as the way to re-enable. Update polls the ini every 2 s even while co-op is disabled. Both edits change tsig, which includes the enabled bit, so each one returns kind 2 and runs ApplyConfigChange, and that nulls _socket. On the next field or world-HUD frame the client builds a new NetSyncSocket on the same _port. Its listener.Start() fails because the old socket is still listening. Mono on Windows sets no SO_REUSEADDR, and even Linux SO_REUSEADDR does not allow a second bind over a live listener. The new instance logs "host loop failed" once and its thread ends. Nothing ever redials it: _socket is reset only by ApplyConfigChange and OnDestroy.

The host's peerLost check is !IsConnected, so the overlay stays on OvlConnecting(0), which reads "waiting for the other player to connect (direct LAN -- they join your IP, port N)". When the guest dials, the old listener accepts. HandleConnection's write loop and read loop both check _running and exit at once, the socket closes, HostLoop leaves its while(_running) loop, and the finally stops the listener. After that the guest's ClientLoop retries every 2 s and is refused every time. Switching LAN to relay and back to LAN, or host to join and back to host, with no guest connected leaves the same leftover listener.

Overstatements:
- "Until relaunch" is too strong. A second off/on cycle after the old listener has exited would bind successfully, but no

The mechanism is real and nothing mitigates it, but "high" overstates the severity. Stop() only sets _running=false and closes _conn. HostLoop's TcpListener is a local variable whose thread is blocked in AcceptSocket(), and nothing ever unblocks it when no peer is connected. So after "Turn co-op off" (Enabled=0 changes tsig and runs ApplyConfigChange, which Stops and nulls _socket), the old thread keeps the port bound. On "Start hosting" (LAN), tsig changes again and Update creates a fresh NetSyncSocket on the same port. Its listener.Start() throws, it logs "host loop failed" once, and the thread exits. NetSyncClient keeps holding this dead, non-null _socket, so it never redials. No watchdog or IsAlive check exists anywhere in Netsync/. The host overlay shows OvlConnecting(0) ("waiting for the other player to connect (direct LAN...)") indefinitely. The guest's first dial is accepted by the zombie and closed straight away, because ReadLoop/WriteLoop gate on _running. The zombie's loop then exits and stops its listener, so every later dial is refused. The trigger is realistic: the Workspace exposes "Turn co-op off" and "Start hosting" as one-click actions, and tutorial 17 even tells users whose games "never pair" to check that nobody clicked Turn co-op off. A second LAN session later in the same game process (after the guest left and stopped dialing) hits this deterministically. The live-connected variant is narrower than claimed. For off-then-on with a guest connected, Stop closes _conn, the old thread exits and releases the port, and the re-enable lands at least one 2 s poll later, so it works. The same-frame race needs a transport-key change with Enabled staying 1 while a guest is connected (e.g. a --new-code rewrite), which is rare. The one-shot sub-claim holds: there is a single outer try at :607-621, and the log line's s.RemoteEndPoint (:615) and s.NoDelay (:649) both sit outside any per-iteration guard. The trigger, though, is a reset between accept and getpeer

findings.title: A session-ending config edit while the guest watches a battle diorama strands it, and the exit ramp then waits on Booted forever
findings.claim: Everything that ends a booted diorama (DioramaTick's watcher leave, hold cap, stall cap and fences 1-2, and EndTick/ExitTick's end-leave) runs only past Update's `if (!_enabled) return;` and past the socket-null early return, and ApplyConfigChange never leaves the diorama. So setting Enabled=0, or changing any transport key, mid-diorama freezes the guest in the battle scene, and the armed exit ramp can never fire because safeToLoad requires !NetSyncDiorama.Booted.
findings.failure_scenario: The host is fighting and the guest watches the diorama. The guest clicks the Workspace's disable-co-op button (coopdoc.disable_coop writes Enabled=0), or edits RelayUrl/SessionCode/Role. LoadConfigIfChanged returns 2, ApplyConfigChange stops the socket and arms the ramp (cause config). Every later Update hits `if (!_enabled) return;` at 1414 (or `_socket == null` with onField false at 1719-1724), so DioramaTick (1946), EndTick (1964) and ReconcileTick never run again. The battle never ends on its own (isDebug keeps IsOver unset), and the ramp at 1351-1353 is blocked by Booted. The guest is stuck in a frozen battle until they know to use ~ then Leave diorama, or kill the game. A variant: FollowHost 1->0 mid-diorama returns at DioramaTick 2141 BEFORE the Booted branch at 2144, so no hold cap or stall cap applies, and if the host then drops, the diorama strands the same way.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:1330-1353 the ramp requires `!NetSyncDiorama.Booted`; :1413-1415 `ServiceFollowWarp(); if (!_enabled) return;`; :1719-1724 `if (_socket == null) { if (!onField && !(onWorld && ...WorldHUD)) return;` (inside a diorama the field is destroyed, so onField is false); :1946 DioramaTick and :1964 EndTick sit after both returns. ApplyConfigChange :1152-1195 stops the socket, resets battle state and arms the ramp, but has no NetSyncDiorama.Leave. :2141-2142 `if (!_followHost) return; // hosts and non-followers never auto-boot` precedes :2144 `if (NetSyncDiorama.Booted)`. NetSyncDiorama.cs:3879 EndTick also returns when !NetSyncBattle.Enabled. Leave's only other callers are the ~ menu (Ff9mkDebugMenu.cs:976-984) and the harness. coopdoc.py:564-570 disable_coop writes {"Enabled": "0"} with no in-battle check.
findings.fix_sketch: In ApplyConfigChange, and in ApplyBehaviorChange's unfollow edge: if NetSyncDiorama.Booted && _dioramaWireNonce >= 0, mark the watcher leave final (_dioramaWatcherLeft/_dioramaWatcherLeftFinal) and call NetSyncDiorama.Leave(), retrying while it defers on a fade. Better: move a minimal 'session over -> leave booted wire diorama' step plus fences 1-2 ahead of the `!_enabled` and socket-null returns. In DioramaTick, move `if (!_followHost) return;` below the Booted branch, since it was only meant to gate auto-boot.

findings.title: A follow-warp racing the guest's own field transition is lost (guest stranded behind a stale _followWarpedTo latch) or replays as a second load
findings.claim: FollowHostTick and ServiceIntentFollow start a follow-warp while the guest's own Field() transition is in flight, and ServiceFollowWarp writes nextMapNo/attr 0.9 s later regardless. A write that lands during the guest's own load is wiped by the new field's init, and the latch then blocks every retry; a write that lands after the guest already reached the same field reloads it a second time.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) STRAND: the host and guest are on A. The guest walks into the door to C while the host takes the door to B. The host's MAPJUMP pushes intent B, and ServiceIntentFollow calls StartFollowWarp(B) mid-gateway (it checks only onField + FieldHUD). The guest's own Field(C) is bounced to a reload of A and shuts the field down that frame. ServiceFollowWarp then fires inside the reload window (after a sync LoadLevel, before HonoUpdate's firstFrame). The A init clears attr bit 8 and resets nextMapNo, so the guest lands on A. _followWarpedTo is still B and the intent nonce is marked seen, so FollowHostTick returns at `rs.Field == _followWarpedTo` forever. The guest stays on A, and the overlay says "following them there..." until the guest presses F11 or the host changes field. The same strand happens when the guest's script MAPJUMP runs in the frame after ServiceFollowWarp's write. (b) DOUBLE LOAD: the guest walks through the same door 0.2-0.5 s behind the host. Intent B starts a follow, and the guest's own Field(B) passes the follow allowance and lands on B. _followWarpPending is still B (FollowHostTick returns early while it is set), so ServiceFollowWarp then calls SetNextMap(B) and sets attr bit 8, and B reloads right after arrival: Main_Init runs twice, with an abrupt second cut.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:3731-3744 FollowHostTick checks onField, FieldHUD, registration and the hold, but not SceneDirector.IsFading/IsReady, FF9Sys.attr&15 or usercontrol. :5388 ServiceIntentFollow has the same gate, then :5398 marks the nonce seen and :5399 calls StartFollowWarp. :3760-3767 StartFollowWarp stamps _followWarpedTo = dest. :5053-5079 ServiceFollowWarp keeps only a mode==3 drop and writes SetNextMap + nextMode=1 + attr|=8 at any time. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:256-266 + 302-314: the guest's own return 4 shuts down and Replaces in the same frame. :445 fldMapNo flips at shutdown. UIManager.SetLoadingForSceneChange (UIManager.cs:571-579) leaves UIState at FieldHUD, so onField and FieldHUD stay true through the guest's own transition. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:203-209: init waits for SceneDirector.IsReady. :80 `FF9Sys.attr &= 0xFFFFFCF0` and :83 `map.nextMapNo = fldMapNo` wipe the follow's write. NetSyncClient.cs:3716 is the latch return. :3709-3713 is the only field-path clear, and it needs co-location. NoteWorldLanding :4259-4263,4288-4289 fixes exactly this 'already warped forever' latch for the WORLD arm only, and NoteGuestWorldJump :4312-4318 cancels a pending field follow when the guest leaves for the world map. No field->field equivalent exists. :8775-8777 is the overlay text.
findings.fix_sketch: (1) Refuse to START a follow (FollowHostTick, ServiceIntentFollow, SameFieldKickTick) while SceneDirector.IsFading or !IsReady, or while (FF9StateSystem.attr & 15) != 0, or while nextMapNo != fldMapNo: a transition of the guest's own is in flight. (2) In ServiceFollowWarp, if a scene change is in flight when the timer expires, keep _followWarpPending and retry after the landing instead of writing. (3) At every field landing (ApplyStoryBeforeEvents), clear _followWarpPending if fld == it, and clear _followWarpedTo when fld != _followWarpedTo, mirroring NoteWorldLanding, so a lost warp re-arms through the serial floor.

The mechanism is real. Nothing in code prevents it, and no ratified decision covers the strand. But "high" overstates it: this is a recoverable stall plus a cosmetic hitch. It is not a softlock and does not touch the save.

Mechanism, traced:

LastHostField hasn't picked up").

On the field path the latch clears only on co-location. ApplyStoryBeforeEvents/NoteWorldLanding clear it only for the world arm, and no field watchdog exists to match WorldArmTimeoutTick.

findings.title: Window events keep ageing out while the guest is paused (KEY TTL is frozen, the inbox TTL is not), so later host choices are lost and auto-picked as Cancel/Default
findings.claim: Purge drops host ADV/CHO events after PendingTtlMs (20 s) of wall time even while the guest is paused, unless their window is already open. A guest that pauses more than 20 s between lines of a host scene therefore loses the host's confirms and choices for every line its script has not opened yet.
findings.failure_scenario: Host and guest are co-located in a host talk: line L1, then a walk beat with no window open, then L2, a Yes/No choice. While its copy sits in the walk beat, the guest presses Start, which is not swallowed because no locked line is open, and stays paused for 25 s. Meanwhile the host picks Yes on L2 (CHO s2) and reads L3 and L4. The guest merges all of them while paused, and each is dropped about 20 s after arrival ('aged out -- no matching window opened'). On unpause, the guest's L2 opens locked with no event. It is held until the host's scene ends plus 2 s, then orphaned and auto-confirmed with CancelChoice, which is 'No' (the host picked Yes). L3 onward are auto-read at roughly 2 s per page, each choice taken as Cancel/Default. The guest's copy diverges from the host's, and on a forced-choice loop it softlocks (next finding).
findings.evidence: GuestTick (NetSyncDialog.cs:1124-1163) calls Purge(ref v) at :1133 every tick, before and regardless of the `paused` read at :1126-1132. Purge :1045-1060 drops an event when `v.Now - e.FirstSeen >= PendingTtlMs && !AwaitedByOpenWindow(e)` (:1053). AwaitedByOpenWindow (:1077-1088) only exempts an event whose window is OPEN. Merge (:879-917, called from NetSyncClient.cs:5867) keeps ingesting while paused, stamping FirstSeen = now at IngestRing :955. By contrast, HoldKeyClocks (:1725-1738) shifts every KEY's FirstSeen forward by the paused delta (:1733-1734), with the rationale at :1717-1724: 'a guest paused past KeyTtlMs mid-scene otherwise lost the host's presses its masked polls were waiting for'. The same reasoning applies to window events, and nothing shifts _inbox. The pause is reachable between lines: UIKeyTrigger.cs:640 and :681-686 route Pause to FieldHUD.OnKeyPause whenever no dialog is active, and the suppress gate at :832 only covers the dialogue path. Orphan choice: Orphans :1517-1527 -> OrphanChoice :1587-1590 (Cancel, else Default). With no explicit cancel, CancelChoice is the LAST option (DialogBoxSymbols.cs:676-678, :689). Secondary: with the KEY TTL frozen, a long pause can also push the KEY list past KeyCap 32. IngestKey :1651-1660 then drops the OLDEST key, which is the one the guest's next poll needs.
findings.fix_sketch: Freeze the inbox TTL exactly as the KEY TTL is frozen: in HoldKeyClocks (or a renamed HoldClocks), also do `_inbox[k].FirstSeen = unchecked(FirstSeen + dt)` while paused. Consider the same while disengaged for a diorama started mid-scene. Optionally make the KEY-list overflow drop the newest key, or skip keys whose reader has no pending poll, rather than the oldest.

- The menu path handles Pause only when no dialog is active.

findings.title: A booted diorama has no exit once co-op is turned off, a transport key changes, or FollowHost is dropped and the link is then cut; the exit ramp also waits on it
findings.claim: Every automatic exit and teardown for the diorama (the watcher, fence 1/2 mop-ups, the hold cap, the end-leave, the reconciler) runs only inside the enabled transport branch, and the watcher's leave logic also needs FollowHost. Any session end other than a link loss therefore freezes the guest inside BattleMapDebug forever, and the exit ramp refuses to fire while it is Booted.
findings.failure_scenario: The guest is watching the host's fight in the diorama. The host quits, or the guest gets bored, and the guest clicks 'Turn off co-op' in the Workspace (coopdoc.disable_coop writes Enabled=0, which the engine hot-reloads). LoadConfig sets _enabled=false and NetSyncBattle.Enabled=false. ApplyConfigChange stops the socket and arms the exit ramp. From then on Update returns at :1414 every frame, so DioramaTick, ReconcileTick and EndTick never run again. The diorama sits with frozen actors and isDebug on, IsOver is never set, and the battle never ends. The exit ramp's safeToLoad requires !NetSyncDiorama.Booted (:1353), so it never fires either. The only way out is the developer ~ menu's 'Leave diorama' or killing the game; per the ~ menu's own comment, the diorama has no stock exit. The same happens on any transport-key edit (role/relay/code/peer): _socket becomes null, and inside the battle scene onField and onWorld are both false, so Update returns at :1722 before DioramaTick. findings.claim: SuppressEncounters is computed from _socket.IsConnected alone (the PEER-ALIVE law forbids this). NetSyncClient.cs:1790 `Boolean connected = _socket.IsConnected;`. 1796 withinGrace keys off _lastConnectedTick, which is stamped on IsConnected. 1802 `suppress = _followHost && (connected || withinGrace || sessionHeld)`. 1808 assigns NetSyncVisitor.SuppressEncounters.

Doc drift: coop.py:731-733 tells the user 'your random encounters pause while paired'.

findings.title: Bridge redials instantly after the relay deliberately REPLACES its leg: two same-code legs evict each other in a tight loop the engines never see
findings.claim: _Upstream.redial treats every upstream EOF as a network wobble and redials immediately with no floor between successful redials. When the relay closes a leg because a second connection with the same code and role registered (relay register() closes the old occupant), the evicted bridge reconnects at once and evicts the other, which does the same, at handshake-RTT rate, while hop-decoupling keeps both games' loopback hops up.
findings.failure_scenario: The host sends their code to a group chat and two friends both click Join, or one friend joins from desktop and laptop, or two hosts end up on one code (finding 3). Guest A's bridge is paired. Guest B's bridge registers as role=guest and the relay closes A's conn (main.go:199-203). A's bridge sees EOF at netsync_bridge.py:580 and calls redial (588), whose first attempt is immediate (465-473, failed=0 every call). It succeeds and closes B's conn, B does the same, and so on: several evictions a second, two log lines per cycle in each bridge's tee file, and TLS handshakes hammering the shared public relay. Neither engine sees a disconnect, because the game hop is never closed. The host's single guest leg alternates between two different players' position, state and command frames, and each guest gets host frames only part of the time (the relay drops frames to an absent partner). The result is co-op desync with no visible error. A game dialing the relay directly would at least see the drop and retry at its 2 s cadence.
findings.evidence: netsync_bridge.py:449-494: redial() resets `failed = 0` on every call; the first open_upstream has no delay and a success returns at once. :571-594: _upstream_to_game calls redial on every _Closed and loops back to read_frame. The module docstring (18-25) assumes every upstream EOF is a 'momentary bridge<->relay wobble'. studies/battle-coop/relay/main.go:190-205: register() runs `sess.guest.conn.Close()` (or host) when the slot is occupied; gorilla Close() sends no close frame, so the bridge cannot tell an eviction from a wobble. The project knows eviction exists (studies/test-harness/multi-instance/RECON.md:51 'it would evict the laptop's leg on the public relay'), but only as a harness hazard.
findings.fix_sketch: Relay: send a WS close frame with an application code (e.g. 4001 'replaced by a newer connection') before closing a replaced leg. Bridge: treat that close code, or N successful redials each lasting under a few seconds inside a window, as TERMINAL. End the session via _end() so the game hop closes and the engine shows the disconnect, and log 'another player is using this session code'. At minimum, put a growing minimum interval between successive successful redials.

votes.reason: I traced the eviction ping-pong end to end and nothing on the path stops it. (1) Every guest dials the same relay slot. The engine builds the path as "/sess/"+code+"?role=guest" for any non-host, and nothing in it identifies the machine. (2) The relay's register() closes whoever already holds that role slot. gorilla's Close() does not send a close frame, so the evicted leg just sees a plain EOF. The old handler's pump then errors, and park() logs "retired (already replaced)" without touching session state. (3) In the evicted bridge, read_frame raises _Closed, stop is not set, and it calls redial(gen). redial resets failed=0 and started/deadline on every call, so the first open_upstream is immediate and a success returns at once. No floor or counter carries over between successful redials, and the 45 s hard cap only applies to consecutive failures, so it never trips. (4) Because everPaired is already true, the relay's handleSession for the new leg goes straight to pump. That new leg evicts the other bridge's leg, which does the same thing back. The cycle runs at roughly handshake-RTT rate (TCP + TLS + upgrade to wss://relay.jawnston.com, the decoded default). (5) _end() is never reached, so the game hop never closes. The engines see no transport drop, and per-guest gaps of a few hundred ms stay under the 2 s staleness windows. RECON.md:51 confirms netsync has no machine identity, and host epochs are host-side only, so the host cannot tell two guests' interleaved frames apart. Both trigger scenarios (two joiners on one code, or one friend on two machines) need only ordinary Join clicks. Severity: I lower it from high to medium. It only fires when the 2-player design is exceeded by a duplicated join, not on the normal path. Even without the bridge, the relay's replace semantics plus the engine's 2 s redial would already thrash. What the bridge adds is a much faster loop, load on the shared public relay, and hiding the problem from the engine. One link I did not trace i

The mechanism is real and nothing guards against it. Bridge side: _upstream_to_game sends every upstream _Closed to redial(). Inside redial(), `failed` is a local reset to 0 on each call, so the first open_upstream fires with no delay. The only wait in the function is stop.wait on a FAILED dial, and a success returns at once, so successive successful redials have no minimum gap. UPSTREAM_REDIAL_HARD_CAP only bounds failures within one call, so the loop never terminates. Relay side: register() unconditionally closes the occupant of the same role slot and installs the newcomer. gorilla Close() sends no close frame, and Caddy only proxies a TCP close, so to the bridge an eviction looks like a wobble. The evicted bridge then redials, registers, and evicts the other leg; that bridge does the same. This ping-pongs about once per TLS+upgrade RTT for as long as both games run. Neither engine notices: the game hop is never closed, and every engine freshness window is 2000-2500 ms, far longer than one flap. The host has no guest identity check either; the F3.3 epoch is host-only and nothing pins a guest Guid. No mitigation exists in the bridge, the relay, the CLI (coop.py has no in-use check), the Workspace, or the engine. Replacing an occupant is a ratified design only for a stale half-open connection (relay README:19-21). The project knows a live same-code leg evicts a peer, but guards that only inside the harness (duo.py:27, instance.py:86-88, RECON.md:51). Severity should be MEDIUM, not high. The trigger is a user error: a third client on a strictly two-player code (code posted to a group chat, or one friend on two machines). The authoritative host's story and save are never mutated by the flapping. Guests are puppets that never autosave while mirroring. Frames stay whole on both hops, so nothing is torn. The harm is a silently garbled session: the ghost jitters between two players, two guests can command the same GuestSlots, and each guest gets a host stream with gaps. I

findings.title: A UTF-8 BOM in Memoria.ini makes the first co-op setup replace the player's whole mod list with just "FF9Coop"
findings.claim: Every ini reader and writer here decodes with plain 'utf-8', which keeps U+FEFF on the first line. A BOM'd '[Mod]' header then fails both `t.startswith("[")` checks, so read_folder_names returns [] and update_ini_section appends a SECOND [Mod] section whose FolderNames = "FF9Coop". The engine's parser strips the BOM and is last-write-wins, so it loads only FF9Coop.
findings.failure_scenario: A player once saved Memoria.ini from an editor that adds a BOM (older Notepad 'UTF-8', Notepad++ 'UTF-8-BOM'), or a tool wrote one, and then runs the first `ff9mapkit coop host` or Workspace 'Start hosting' before the launcher rewrites the file. ensure_room -> find_registered_field reads FolderNames as [], so it checks only FF9Coop and builds the room there even if another active folder already registers 30003. ensure_folder_registered -> mod_order_updates(text, [] + ['FF9Coop']) writes `\r\n[Mod]\r\nFolderNames = "FF9Coop"` at EOF. Probe result: the engine-equivalent parse gives FolderNames = "FF9Coop". On the next launch, Moguri, FF9CustomMap, the -world overworld and every other mod are inactive, and a save standing on a custom field id boots to a black screen. The kit says only 'added FF9Coop'.
findings.evidence: coop.py:409 and :458 use `read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")`, and the 'utf-8' codec does not strip a BOM. :252-256 (read_ini_key): `t = line.strip()`; str.strip() keeps U+FEFF, so `t.startswith("[")` is False for the first header. :362-368 is the same test in update_ini_section, so the section is never found and :382-387 appends a new `[Mod]`. Memoria IniFile.Init (Assembly-CSharp/Memoria/Configuration/IniFile.cs:90-123) uses a StreamReader, which strips the BOM, and `Options[new Key(section,key)] = value` is last-wins. find_registered_field (:481) uses the same empty FolderNames. Contrast :484, which reads DictionaryPatch.txt with 'utf-8-sig'. Verified with bom_probe.py in the scratchpad.
findings.fix_sketch: Read with encoding='utf-8-sig' everywhere coop.py and the harness overlay read Memoria.ini, or strip a leading '﻿' in _split_lines/read_ini_key and write it back if it was present. Add a regression test with a BOM'd ini that asserts FolderNames keeps its existing entries and that only one [Mod] header exists after ensure_folder_registered.

findings.title: Silent no-pair over the relay: a wire-version mismatch is dropped without a signal, and the host's overlay says 'connected' with no peer at all
findings.claim: On the relay path every frame from a different-version peer is silently discarded, so the session looks like it never pairs. On the host, peerLost is the bare transport test, so with the local bridge up the host is told 'connected -- waiting for your friend to arrive on this screen' whether or not any guest exists. Neither machine can tell a version mismatch, a wrong code or an absent friend apart.
findings.failure_scenario: The host runs the b22 engine (wire v14) and the guest still has an older bundle. Both start the bridges with the same code, and the relay pairs and forwards. Every frame fails TryParseHeader on both sides and is dropped with no log line. The guest sees 'the bridge is up -- waiting for the host's game ... check the host is in: ff9mapkit coop host'. The host sees 'FF9 co-op: connected -- waiting for your friend to arrive on this screen'. Both conclude the other is in the wrong place, and nothing points at the engine version. A wrong code or a guest who never launched gives the host the same false 'connected'. On direct TCP the mismatch is at least logged, but it reconnects every 2 s forever (3 log lines per cycle on each side) and the host's overlay flickers between 'waiting for the other player' and 'connected'.
findings.evidence: NetSyncRelay.cs:346-363: `if (NetSyncWire.TryParseHeader(payload, out type, out flen) && flen == payload.Length - NetSyncWire.HeaderSize) { ... _frames.Accept(type, body); }` with no else-branch. The comment admits it: 'this transport gives no signal -- a v-mismatch over the relay looks like a session that never pairs' (:348-353). TryParseHeader rejects on `buf[1] != Version` (NetSyncSocket.cs:185). Host overlay: `Boolean peerLost = _role == "client" ? !(rs.Valid && _socket.IsConnected) : !_socket.IsConnected;` (NetSyncClient.cs:1814). With the bridge hop up, peerLost=false and rs.Valid=false, so the chain falls through to the else at :1917-1923, then FieldWaitTail, then OvlWaiting (:4688-4691). That text is 'FF9 co-op: connected -- waiting for your friend to arrive on this screen' (:8771-8773). The host never composes the detail-1 'hop up, no peer' text (:8751-8758: 'a host always composes these'). TCP: 'peer speaks a different wire version -- disconnecting' (NetSyncSocket.cs:682), followed by ClientLoop's 2 s retry (:642).
findings.fix_sketch: WIRE-5: in NetSyncRelay.ReadLoop, count header rejects where payload[0]==Magic and record payload[1] as PeerWireVersion on INetTransport (also in NetSyncSocket before disconnecting). Show an overlay state 'your friend runs wire vN, you run v14 -- update both machines', and back the TCP redial off once a mismatch is seen. For the host, compose OvlWaiting's 'connected' wording only when rs.Valid. Otherwise show 'relay up -- waiting for your friend to join (code X)'. This changes overlay text only, so S120-R1's behaviour-identity for the ghost and grace logic is kept. Status: PLAN.md:188 deferred this ('optional harden later'), F3.2-DESIGN.md:1030 lists WIRE-5 as a suggestion, and S120-R1 deliberately kept the host on the transport test. That acceptance reasoned about behaviour identity, not about the overlay text, which has been wrong on the relay path since the bridge.

findings.title: Public relay has no message-size limit or connection caps, so one client can exhaust its memory and drop every live session
findings.claim: The relay never calls SetReadLimit, so gorilla's ReadMessage buffers an arbitrarily large message with io.ReadAll. There is also no per-IP or total connection cap, no code-length cap, and CheckOrigin accepts every origin, while the one in-memory process serves every co-op session.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone (no code needed: they mint their own) opens host+guest legs with a random code, pairs them, and sends one WebSocket message with a multi-GB length header. pump's ReadMessage grows a buffer until the relay is OOM-killed. Every paired session worldwide drops; the in-memory session map is lost, and bridges redial into fresh sessions for up to their 45 s hard cap. Repeating it keeps the service down. A low-rate variant holds thousands of unpaired upgraded connections, each a goroutine for 60 s. CheckOrigin=true also lets any web page drive this from visitors' browsers.
findings.evidence: `var upgrader = websocket.Upgrader{ CheckOrigin: func(*http.Request) bool { return true } }` (main.go:52-55). `conn, err := upgrader.Upgrade(w, r, nil)` with no SetReadLimit anywhere in the file (:113-118). pump: `mt, data, err := own.conn.ReadMessage()` (:220). gorilla's default readLimit is 0 (unlimited), and ReadMessage = NextReader + io.ReadAll. The code is taken unbounded from the path: `code := strings.ToUpper(strings.SplitN(rest, "/", 2)[0])` (:102). Downstream caps are tighter: the bridge stops at 1 MiB per frame (netsync_bridge.py:108, :392-393) and the engine at 1 MiB per WS message / 8192 per NetSync frame (NetSyncRelay.cs:322, NetSyncSocket.cs:155). So the relay is the only unbounded hop, and it is shared.
findings.fix_sketch: Call `conn.SetReadLimit(64 << 10)` right after Upgrade: legitimate frames are at most about 8.2 KB, so this is generous. Reject codes over ~64 chars and non-matching roles BEFORE Upgrade. Cap concurrent connections per remote IP (Caddy forwards X-Forwarded-For; trust it only from 127.0.0.1) and in total. Refuse requests carrying a browser Origin header (game and bridge clients send none).

votes.reason:
The path is reachable end to end with no authentication, but the failure scenario overstates how easy it is in two places.

How the attack works:
- The default relay URL ships publicly in the PyPI bridge (the obfuscated value decodes to wss://relay.jawnston.com).
- The relay checks only that the code is non-empty and the role is host or guest. Pairing needs nothing more than two legs with the same code, so an attacker can mint their own session.
- Once paired, each leg's handler runs pump(), which calls gorilla's ReadMessage. ReadMessage is NextReader plus io.ReadAll, and SetReadLimit is never called anywhere in main.go. gorilla's readLimit defaults to 0 (no limit), so a single message, including continuation frames, collects in memory without bound.
- All session state is one in-memory map in one process. If that process dies, every live pairing is lost.
- Downstream hops do cap the size: the bridge stops at 1 MiB per WS frame (netsync_bridge.py:108, :392-393), NetSyncRelay.cs:322 caps WS frames at 1<<20, and NetSyncSocket.cs:155 sets MaxPayload=8192. That makes the relay the only unbounded hop, as the reviewer said.

Corrections to the failure scenario:
1. A multi-GB length header allocates nothing by itself. io.ReadAll grows the buffer only as bytes actually arrive. The read deadline (idleTimeout, 90 s) is set before ReadMessage and only refreshed after a whole message completes (lines 218 and 224), so one message has 90 s to grow. Peak memory is therefore about the attacker's upload rate times 90 s, summed over however many pairs they open, plus ReadAll's growth copies and Go's heap slack (GOGC). That is easy to sustain: about 100 Mbps gives about 1.1 GB live per window, and a repeat attack keeps the relay down. But it is a bandwidth attack, not a single-packet kill.
2. The low-rate variant of holding thousands of unpaired connections is weak. An unpaired leg is never read, because its handler is parked in the select at lines 133-152. Each one costs a goroutine

Unpaired legs are never read (main.go:133-152). The bridges' 45 s same-code redial (netsync_bridge.py:102) may heal a single crash if systemd restarts the relay quickly. votes.reason:
The defect is real. The repo copy of the relay never calls SetReadLimit, I found no ratified decision accepting it, and no guard further down stops the relay from running out of memory. But the failure scenario overstates the impact, and the fix sketch needs two corrections.

What holds:
- The relay uses gorilla v1.5.1 with its default read limit of 0 (no limit). ReadMessage is NextReader followed by io.ReadAll, so one paired leg can make the single shared process buffer a message of any size. That behaviour comes from my knowledge of the library: there is no local module cache to check it against.
- Nothing upstream bounds it. Caddy is a bare reverse_proxy, and the systemd unit sets no MemoryMax, TasksMax or LimitNOFILE.
- Pairing needs no authority. register() creates a session for any code, so an attacker can mint a code and pair both legs themselves.
- There is a cheaper second vector. The 90 s read deadline is reset only after each complete message, so a pair that sends a tiny message every 89 s stays alive forever. With no per-IP or total cap, an attacker can stack such pairs without limit.
- The blast radius is wider than co-op. The same relay is the hard-coded default for JawnRPG's netcode too, and the VPS also serves jawnston.com, feedback and umami.

What is overstated:
1. A multi-GB length header alone allocates nothing. io.ReadAll grows only as bytes actually arrive, and the whole message must land within the 90 s deadline. So the memory an attacker can force is about their bandwidth times 90 s (roughly 1 GB per connection at 100 Mbps, times about 2 for slice growth and GC). A cheap cloud VM can still OOM a small Hetzner box, especially with parallel pairs.
2. Unpaired legs are never read: handleSession blocks in the pairing select before pump. So the "thousands of unpaired connections" variant costs only goroutines and buffers held for 60 s, not message memory.
3. Each crash heals in seconds rather than causing a sustained outage. systemd has Restart=on
votes.mitigated_by: Partial only, and none of it prevents the OOM. The 90 s read deadline (main.go:48, :218/:224) caps how much one message can accumulate at about 90 s of attacker bandwidth. systemd Restart=on-failure with RestartSec=2 (jawn-relay.service:11-12) plus the bridge's immediate redial with a 45 s cap (netsync_bridge.py:103, :449-494) heal each crash in seconds, because both legs re-register the same code. Unguessable ff9-plus-8 codes rule out targeted attacks, and direct TCP/LAN co-op does not use the relay. There is no read limit, connection cap or cgroup memory cap anywhere.

findings.title: Latest-slot lanes re-send the full 2-5 KB story-state (and roster) every 33 ms, about 0.7-1.2 Mbit/s sustained, which backs up on weak links and through the relay
findings.claim: CollectOutgoing appends every non-null latest slot on every write tick whether it changed or not. The host's type-5 frame (2048 B gEventGlobal + party/key-item/bag sections + section 7 ring) leaves 30 times a second, and with no pacing or change detection a constrained uplink, downlink or relay leg turns the excess into a growing TCP backlog behind which every lane lags.
findings.failure_scenario: The host plays from a laptop on a mediocre uplink (or a phone hotspot). Its type-5 frame is about 4 KB late-game (2051 story + about 550 party + about 200 key items + 4 B per bag item + about 430 section 7), so 30 Hz is about 120 KB/s, plus about 2 KB roster during battles. When the uplink saturates, kernel buffers fill and the engine writer blocks inside stream.Write. Position, dialogue-ring and command frames then reach the guest seconds late: the ghost rubber-bands, follow-warps lag, picks arrive after the 2.5 s refusal window and buzz as REFUSED. Through the relay the same volume crosses the server twice per session. If the guest's downlink is the slow side, back-pressure through Caddy can trip the relay's 5 s write deadline, which parks the guest and closes its conn. That matches the 'upstream EOFs every 10-36 s' the bridge was hardened against, but it is unverified; check the relay journal for 'guest parked (write failed: ... i/o timeout)'.
findings.evidence: `if (_outPos != null) into.Add(_outPos); if (_outBattle != null) into.Add(_outBattle); ... if (_outRoster != null) into.Add(_outRoster); if (_outState != null) into.Add(_outState);` every tick (NetSyncSocket.cs:355-359). The writers loop with `Thread.Sleep(33)` (NetSyncSocket.cs:707, NetSyncRelay.cs:269), and stream.Write has no SendTimeout. Size: StoryLen = 2048 (NetSyncState.cs:45), the party/key/bag sections (NetSyncParty.cs:99-192; bag = 4 B per distinct item, :184-185), and section 7 appended to every host frame (NetSyncClient.cs:5181-5183). Relay: `writeTimeout = 5 * time.Second` (main.go:43), and a write failure parks the partner and closes its conn (:239-255). The design doc's own estimate is '~90 KB/s of identical state re-sends (WIRE-7)' (studies/field-coop/F3.2-DESIGN.md:656, :1030).
findings.fix_sketch: WIRE-7: give each latest slot a dirty flag (or compare to the last-sent array). Send a slot on change plus a 2-4 Hz keepalive, keeping pos at 30 Hz as the liveness lane. The section-7 ring already tolerates loss across ticks, which is what makes this safe. Before tuning, grep the relay journal for write-deadline parks to confirm or kill the 'EOFs every 10-36 s' hypothesis.

The mechanism is real in the live tree and nothing guards it. The host rebuilds its type-5 frame at about 7 Hz (every 150 ms), with out-of-band pushes on top. The frame goes into a latest slot that is never cleared and never compared. CollectOutgoing then appends that slot, along with every other non-null latest slot, on every 33 ms write tick, so about 4-5 identical copies leave per rebuild.

The frame is roughly 2.9-3.7 KB:
- the 2051 B story section
- party sections at about 70 B plus 4 B per support ability, per slot
- key items at 2 B each and the bag at 4 B per distinct item
- section 7 up to 424 B (12 + 24 + 1 + 32x12 when the ring is full)
- the small sections 5 and 8

So on any link that cannot sustain about 1 Mbit/s (a hotspot, contended Wi-Fi, or a host screen-sharing on the same uplink), position, dialogue, intent and battle frames queue behind the stale state copies. The host-to-guest lane matters most: the guest's 2500 ms MirrorRefuseMs reads the host's Ready bit off the battle lane, so a seconds-late stream can turn into false REFUSED verdicts. 1. The lag is bounded by the buffer depth (the kernel send buffer, the bridge's two hops, and Caddy/server buffers on the relay path) divided by the link rate. That is seconds on a weak link, not an ever-growing backlog. A sustained block can also DROP queued commands at the cap.

findings.title: The exit ramp reloads an autosave that is older than the pre-session state; the docs claim a capture that does not exist
findings.claim: The ramp's premise, that 'the Continue slot IS the coherent pre-session (story, position, party) tuple', is false in ordinary play. Battle returns never autosave, autosave is suppressed from the moment the guest connects to the bridge, and AutoSaveOnlyAtMoogle/DisableAutoSave freeze it further. The party/bag/gil mirror is read-wrap only, so the guest's real pre-session party, EXP and items stay in memory through the session and are discarded by the Autoload. ApplyStoryBeforeEvents' comment says the first mirror 'Captures the guest's own story', but no code captures anything.
findings.failure_scenario: The guest grinds random battles for 30 minutes on one field (each return goes through the reinit branch, so no autosave), opens a chest, then pairs with the host. It follows, mirrors and plays. When the session ends, ExitMirrorToOwnSave loads the field-entry autosave from before the grind, and the 30 minutes of EXP, gil and items are silently gone. Under [SaveFile] AutoSaveOnlyAtMoogle=1 the guest is thrown back to its last moogle field. Under DisableAutoSave=1 it gets an arbitrarily old autosave, or the title. The user doc only says 'your game reloads your own autosave'.
findings.evidence: NetSyncState.cs:182-191 claims the 'coherent pre-session (story, position, party) tuple'. NetSyncClient.cs:698-702 'Captures the guest's own story on the first mirror (the spectator-save bracket)', but ApplyStoryImpl at 766-774 only sets _storyMirroring and captures nothing. WinIosAndrSharedDataSerializer.cs:92-93 Autosave returns when DisableAutoSave is set. NetSyncParty.cs:38-40: real party/bag are never touched by the mirror. tutorials/17-coop.md:65. findings.fix_sketch: At the first live pairing, while the guest is still free-standing on its OWN field before any follow-warp, force one Autosave of its own state (or take an in-memory JSON with Parser.ParseFromFF9StateSystem), and have the ramp restore that snapshot with ParseToFF9StateSystem plus ReplaceLoadMap. Warn when AutoSaveOnlyAtMoogle/DisableAutoSave is set. Fix both comments.

findings.title: The ending escapes the save guards: the game-finish flag and the CompleteGame/Blackjack achievements reach disk and later Steam
findings.claim: The achievement gate sits in ProcessAchievementReport, but ReportAchievement first calls SetAchievementStatus(ReadyToUnlock), and for the two system achievements that writes the save file's metadata at once. Every later ResyncSystemAchievements at the title or on launch then reports them once the guest is no longer mirroring. EndingMain's SetGameFinishFlagWithTrue has no co-op gate at all. A following guest reaches EndingMain because the gateway bounce budget lets Field(16000) through after 3 bounces.
findings.failure_scenario: The host finishes the game, and the guest follows into Ending/TH (field 3011). Its copy of Dagger_Queen_Loop waits about 267 frames and calls Field(16000). LastHostField is 0 (the host is in the Ending scene), so RedirectGuestFieldJump bounces to a same-field reload; each pass takes about 10 s, inside the 20 s window. On the 4th call `_bounceStreak >= MaxBounceStreak` lets it through, and the guest enters EndingMain. There SetGameFinishFlagWithTrue sets metadata IsGameFinishFlag=1, which unlocks the title's Movie and Blackjack buttons on the guest's install. ReportAchievement(CompleteGame) persists SystemAchievementStatuses=ReadyToUnlock to disk, and Blackjack does the same. On the next launch (Social.Authenticate) or title return after the session, ResyncSystemAchievements reports them to Steam, which the funnel comment says can never happen.
findings.evidence: AchievementManager.cs:81-88: ReportAchievement calls `SetAchievementStatus(key, ReadyToUnlock)` before ProcessAchievementReport; :42-64: for system keys it calls `FF9StateSystem.Serializer.SetSystemAchievementStatuses(...)`, and SharedDataBytesStorage.cs:1038-1065 writes metadata to the save file; :113 is the only co-op gate, inside ProcessAchievementReport. AchievementState.cs:77-80 lists the system keys CompleteGame and Blackjack. AchievementManager.cs:247-259 resync reports ReadyToUnlock; it is called from TitleUI.cs:1298-1301 and Social.cs:86-89. EndingMain.cs:85-91 calls SetGameFinishFlagWithTrue plus ReportAchievement(CompleteGame) ungated; TitleUI.cs:1119-1129 uses the flag to unlock the extras. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:257-261 and 341-342 send Field(16000) to the Ending scene. NetSyncClient.cs:246-247 (MaxBounceStreak 3, 20000 ms) and :442-453 let the jump through. test2_806.txt:430-443 (field 3011): Wait(180), Wait(60), Wait(25), Wait(2), Field(16000).
findings.fix_sketch: Move the `HoldAchievement || IsMirroringStory` check to the top of ReportAchievement, before SetAchievementStatus, and gate EndingMain's SetGameFinishFlagWithTrue and its ReportAchievement on !IsMirroringStory. In RedirectGuestFieldJump, never let the budget pass dest == FF9Define.FLDSCRPT_EVTNO_ENDING; hold the guest on the field (or ramp it out) instead.

findings.title: Encounter and autosave suppression key on IsConnected, so behind the bridge they stay on with no live host (before pairing and after the exit ramp)
findings.claim: SuppressEncounters is `_followHost && (_socket.IsConnected || grace || sessionHeld)`. Behind the relay bridge IsConnected is the hop to the local bridge (the PEER-ALIVE law). A guest with no live host therefore keeps random encounters off, and its field-load autosave off, while it plays its OWN save.
findings.failure_scenario: A guest runs `ff9mapkit coop join` and plays while waiting for the host, or the host quits mid-session: the session grace expires, the exit ramp autoloads the guest's own save, and the guest keeps playing alone with the bridge still running. In both cases the bridge socket stays connected, so IsNoEncounter is true and the autosave is skipped (EventEngine.cs:693). The guest crosses dungeons with no random battles, and can manually save that progress, because the save gate keys on IsMirroringStory, which is false here. A crash loses everything since the last manual save, because no autosave ran.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:1790 `Boolean connected = _socket.IsConnected;` and :1802 `suppress = _followHost && (connected || withinGrace || sessionHeld);`. :1797-1800 even notes 'behind the bridge `connected` already holds it'. SettingsState.cs:53-54 makes IsNoEncounter include SuppressEncounters. EventEngine.cs:693 `noSave |= SuppressEncounters || IsMirroringStory`. The memory brief records the PEER-ALIVE law (IsConnected != peer alive), and the s55 comment's 'a real link loss un-pauses after the grace' is false behind the bridge.
findings.fix_sketch: Compute `connected` as peer-alive for a client (`_socket.IsConnected && _socket.GetRemote().Valid`, as sessionPeerAlive at :1490 already does), keeping the grace and sessionHeld extensions. Better still, scope the pause to IsLiveFollowedSession || _storyMirroring || SessionGrace, so a waiting or post-ramp guest is vanilla.

I traced the path end to end in the live tree and the finding holds. A guest set up by `coop join` (FollowHost=1, RelayUrl pointing at the local bridge) dials as soon as it stands on a field, and no peer is needed for that. The bridge sends the 101 to the game as soon as the public relay accepts the upgrade. The relay upgrades at once and only then waits up to 60 s for pairing. So IsConnected goes true before any host exists. When the pairing wait runs out, or the host leaves, the relay closes the guest's leg. The bridge then redials only the upstream hop and never touches the game hop, and its 45 s hard cap only fires while dials keep failing, which they don't while the relay is up. findings.title: The orphan rule's Cancel pick live-locks the guest on stock forced-choice re-ask loops
findings.claim: An orphaned choice is always auto-committed with CancelChoice (the last option by default). In stock loops that re-open the same choice on that option, the guest's copy re-asks itself forever, about every 4 s, with its input swallowed throughout.

findings.claim: Only the warm field return and the world return stop a battle song still playing over the suspended field/world song. findings.claim: ValidateWireBoot only proves that the scene id, its SceneData key, dbfile0000.raw16 and the pattern index exist. findings.claim: NetSyncSocket.Stop() sets _running=false and closes only the accepted _conn. The listener is a local in HostLoop, blocked in AcceptSocket(), and _running is re-checked only after a connection arrives. With no guest connected, the old listener stays bound on IPAddress.Any after co-op is turned off, and the replacement socket that ApplyConfigChange makes cannot bind the same port.

findings.title: A former guest's stored SessionCode (the friend's invite) is silently reused as this PC's own host code
findings.claim: `coop join X` stores the host's code X as SessionCode. A later `coop host` on that PC reuses whatever SessionCode is stored, and so does the Workspace, whose read-only host code field is seeded from the ini. findings.failure_scenario: Night 1: A hosts with code X and B joins with X (B's ini: SessionCode = X). Night 2: B hosts for C (CLI `coop host` or Workspace 'Start hosting') and gets X again. Even without overlap, B's 'private invite link' is a code A, and anyone A gave it to, already holds, so they can join B's session and command the party slots B hands out.

findings.title: Relay 'replace the stale occupant' plus the bridge's immediate redial livelocks whenever two live clients share a code and role
findings.claim: register() unconditionally closes whatever leg holds the role slot, assuming it is half-open. The evicted client's bridge treats the close as an upstream EOF and redials with zero delay, because the backoff applies only after failed dials. Two live same-role clients therefore evict each other in a tight loop forever, and both keep enough fresh frames to look paired.
findings.failure_scenario: The host shares the code with two friends (a 3-player attempt), or a guest mistakenly runs `coop host ff9-XXXX` with the host's code, or one person runs `coop join` on two PCs. Client A holds the guest slot. B registers, and the relay closes A's conn. A's bridge sees EOF, redials at once (TLS + upgrade, about 100-300 ms) and evicts B. B's bridge does the same, and so on at about 3-10 evictions per second, with relay and bridge logs growing without bound. Both guests' loopback hops stay up, and each gets host frames in sub-second bursts under StaleMs=2000, so PEER-ALIVE holds on BOTH. Both follow-warp to the host, both mirror the host's story, both boot dioramas and send picks for the same GuestSlots. The host's single ghost jumps between the two guests' positions. Nobody is told why.
findings.evidence: main.go:190-205: `case "guest": if sess.guest != nil { replaced = true; sess.guest.conn.Close() } sess.guest = self` -- no liveness test on the occupant. The design note says the replace is for a 'half-open stale connection' (main.go:15-17), but the call site never checks staleness: a law in a docstring. Bridge: on `_Closed`, `_upstream_to_game` calls `self.up.redial(gen)` (netsync_bridge.py:580-594). redial makes an immediate attempt; on success it returns with no sleep (:468-494). `_REDIAL_BACKOFFS` is consulted only in the failure branch (:474-486). Engine side: the hop stays up (decoupled), and PEER-ALIVE is `rs.Valid && IsConnected` with a 2000 ms staleness (NetSyncSocket.cs:265, :418-426; NetSyncClient.cs:1814). Eviction itself is known only as a harness rule ('never the owner's live code (it would evict the laptop's leg on the public relay)', studies/test-harness/multi-instance/RECON.md:50). The tug-of-war consequence is not documented.
findings.fix_sketch: Relay: stamp a lastRead time per leg in pump. In register, replace the occupant only if it has been silent for more than ~3 s (a genuinely stale conn). Otherwise refuse the newcomer: an HTTP 409 before Upgrade, or a WS close 4009 'seat taken'. Bridge: treat an upstream that dies within ~2 s of a successful dial as a failure for backoff purposes, and pass a relay close reason through so the engine overlay can say 'another player already holds this seat'.

votes.reason: I traced the mechanism end to end and it holds. The relay's register() closes whatever leg holds the role slot without checking whether it is alive. The evicted bridge reads that close as an upstream EOF and redials with no delay, because backoff applies only to FAILED dials, and the new dial evicts the other client in turn. No guard stops this. The relay has no liveness test and no per-peer identity, the bridge has no minimum time between successful redials, and the engine never notices because the game<->bridge hop stays up. Each holder keeps its seat for about one dial round trip (TCP + TLS + upgrade, a few hundred ms). That keeps both guests' remote-position lanes well under StaleMs=2000, so PEER-ALIVE (IsConnected && GetRemote().Valid) holds on BOTH machines. Meanwhile the host's pump sends to whichever leg holds sess.guest at that moment, and the host's single ghost takes its position from whichever leg is currently forwarding. The triggers are real CLI inputs: `coop join <code>` takes any code, and `coop host` also takes a code override. Two things soften the finding. First, it needs an unsupported setup: a third player, the same person joining from two PCs, or a second host using an existing code. Second, it ends on its own once either duplicate leaves. A clean quit tears the session down; an abrupt quit parks that leg, and the survivor's next redial takes the seat. The bridge console does print repeated redial lines, so the loop is not fully silent. It is never explained to the user as 'seat taken', though. Nothing persistent is damaged: following guests never autosave while mirroring, and the host's playthrough is just its own game with two people sending picks. The relay log grows by about 3 lines per cycle and each bridge log by 2, for as long as the loop runs (journald rate-limits the server side). I rate it low, not medium: the mechanism is real, but it fires only on misuse and it heals itself.
votes.mitigated_by: Nothing prevents the loop. Its impact is bounded by three things. It needs an unsupported 3rd-seat or duplicate-join setup. It heals itself once either duplicate leaves: a clean WS close tears the session down (main.go:158-163), and an abrupt quit parks that leg so the survivor's next redial holds the seat. Followers never autosave while mirroring, so no save is corrupted.

findings.title: A pending exit ramp survives a trip to the title and yanks the player out of the save or New Game they just chose
findings.claim: Only the ramp's own fire clears _exitRampPending and _storyMirroring; the title arrival does not. If the session ends while the guest is at the title (or the guest reaches the title before the ramp could fire), a title Load, Continue or New Game lands with IsMirroringStory still true. findings.title: The bounce budget's 20 s sliding window cannot stop an auto-transition loop whose period exceeds 20 s
findings.claim: The budget meant to stop a field whose script auto-calls Field() from reloading FOREVER only counts bounces that come less than 20 s apart. A cutscene that runs more than 20 s before its Field() resets the streak to 1 on every bounce, so the let-through never happens.
findings.failure_scenario: The guest is on a story field whose Main_Init cutscene (more than 20 s) ends in Field(Y), and the host is not on Y: on the world map, in a battle, on a field this install lacks, at the title, or during the PreEnding chain. Each Field(Y) bounces into a reload of the field, the cutscene replays, and 20+ s later it bounces again with `_bounceStreak = 1`. The guest replays the cutscene indefinitely, with only the follow-warp able to break it, and that only once the host stands on a registered field while the guest is on FieldHUD.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:237-250: the comment promises the budget stops reload-forever; MaxBounceStreak=3, BounceStreakWindowMs=20000. :442 `if (_lastBounceField == myField && now - _lastBounceTick <= BounceStreakWindowMs)` increments the streak, otherwise :456-460 resets it to 1. :461 stamps _lastBounceTick at every bounce, so the gap is measured bounce to bounce, and a period over 20 s never accumulates. The follow-warp floor is blocked for rs.Field <= 0 (:3704-3707), an unregistered field (:3737-3738), not FieldHUD (:3735) and the hold (:3739-3743).
findings.fix_sketch: Count consecutive bounces on the same field with no intervening user-input field change, not by wall-clock gap. For example, keep the streak while every bounce happens without the guest having had control since the reload (a no-input auto-transition), or measure from the bounce reload's landing to the next jump and treat a jump the guest never steered toward as auto. Let the jump through after N, and log once.

findings.title: A handed-back (Local) script-polled line is masked again as soon as the host gets busy, because the key lock is per field, not per window

The guest's press reaches Dialog.OnKeyConfirm, which is a no-op on an Inh window. The page freezes for the whole host talk plus 2 s. UpdateChip ignores Local windows, so the guest sees no chip, or only 'the host is in a scene'. In the re-rise variant, the host's first KEY on that field clears _ownPollsField, and from then on the guest's Local polled choice is committed by the HOST's press with the GUEST's highlight (ApplyKeyCursor returns CurOwn, which KeyCursorSettled serves at once).

findings.title: Digit-panel target and item picks are index-based and re-derived at keypress; a death or count change between draw and press lands the pick on another unit (friendly fire) or another item
findings.claim: The digit panel resolves '[k]' against a candidate list (enemies first, then party) or the item list. Both are rebuilt from the live view and roster at the moment of the keypress, so any shift between what the player read and the press moves the pick onto a different unit or item. The host retargets only when NO living unit is in the mask, and allies always count as living.
findings.failure_scenario: The Attack target list reads [1] Goblin A, [2] Goblin B, [3] Zidane... The guest reads it and presses [2] for Goblin B, but Goblin A dies a moment before the press. The list is now [1] Goblin B, [2] Zidane, so the frame carries Zidane's bit. The host's maskHasLiving is true for any player bit, so the guest's character attacks Zidane (often the host's own leader). The same happens on item pages: the host uses its last Potion, the next roster (RosterMs) drops it, and the guest's [3] now uses the Elixir that slid into that position.
findings.evidence: RunAssistUi UiTarget 4737-4747: `List<UnitView> targets = TargetCandidates(view, _pendTargetType, _pendForDead); ... BuildCommand(..., (UInt16)(1 << targets[idx].Index), 0)`. The list is computed at keypress time. TargetCandidates 4809-4835 lists enemies (pass 0) and then players (pass 1), filtering dead units out. Attack's SingleAny allows both sides (4811-4812). UiItem 4722-4732 indexes `roster.Items[idx]` from the current roster. AppendMenu 7393-7403 and 7376-7391 draw from the same live data each frame, so the layout shifts under the player's finger. Host HandleCommandPayload 5943-5944: `if ((mask & (1 << idx)) != 0 && (u.CurrentHp > 0 || u.IsPlayer)) maskHasLiving = true;`. The retarget at 5990-5991 fires only when !maskHasLiving. The stock HUD cursor binds to a unit, not a list position.
findings.fix_sketch: Snapshot the candidate unit indices (and the item ids of the open page) when the target or item mode is entered, and draw from that snapshot. On keypress, check that the snapshot entry is still a valid, alive candidate. If not, buzz and redraw instead of sending. Optionally send the pick only if the unit at that position is the same Index that was drawn.

Pump can also adopt a newer view in the same Update, just before it reads the key.

Attack really is SingleAny (Actions.csv row 176, SingleAny(0)). So after the enemies, TargetCandidates lists the living party, with slot 0 (usually the host's leader) first. A [2] press after Goblin A dies therefore sends 1<<0. On the host, maskHasLiving counts any player bit, so the retarget is skipped. findings.title: A field guest paired while the host is off-field arms the host's story on its first warm diorama return: Main_Reinit runs the guest's own-story field with the host's flags
findings.claim: When the host is on the world map at pairing time (routine since decision 9) the guest's mirror stays unarmed. The first host battle's FIELD diorama primes a warm copy of the guest's OWN-story field. ApplyStoryBeforeEvents then applies the host snapshot on that warm-return load, so StartEvents' reinit branch restores the own-story ctx0 and runs Main_Reinit under the host's gEventGlobal. That is the mid-field mirror-arm frankenstate the s42 design rejected.
findings.failure_scenario: The guest Continues a disc-1 field save in Lindblum; the host Continues a disc-3 world-map save. The host's position lane reads field 0, so the guest neither follows nor gets a kick, and its mirror stays unarmed. The host draws a world encounter. The guest boots a field diorama: own party (finding 1's field leg), WARM primed (WarmVerdict has no mirror input). On Leave the field load runs ApplyStoryBeforeEvents, then ApplyStoryImpl overwrites gEventGlobal with the host's disc-3 story and sets _storyMirroring = true. StartEvents then takes the reinit branch (ctx1 inited 1, lastmap == fld), restores the disc-1 field's objects and MAP vars, and runs Main_Reinit against disc-3 flags. Field polls and ATEs then read a story the field's objects were never built for, so a branch can wedge or start a foreign event. Saves are blocked from then on, so the permanent save is safe, but the field can softlock until the next follow or the exit ramp.
findings.evidence:
- ApplyStoryBeforeEvents (NetSyncClient.cs:703-721) runs BeforeFieldEvents, then ApplyStoryImpl, on EVERY field load. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:149-150 calls it right before StartEvents, the warm return included.
- ApplyStoryImpl (742-774) applies whenever the guest is following and connected and a snapshot exists, and arms `_storyMirroring = true`. It has no warm-return exception.
- PrimeWarmReturn's WarmVerdict inputs (NetSyncDiorama.cs:1384-1392) include no mirror state. It copies ctx0 into ctx1 at 1399-1400.
- StartEvents' reinit branch is EventEngine.cs:667-672.
- The kick that exists to arm the mirror before the first battle fires only when co-located (NetSyncClient.cs:3709-3714, 5020-5025).
- The memory file records 'Mid-field mirror-arm was REJECTED (the exit-ramp law's frankenstate class, in reverse)'.
- The same holds when the host is in a field battle at pairing (field 0). Decision 9 makes host-off-field-at-pairing the normal case.
findings.fix_sketch:
Two parts:
- When paired with !_storyMirroring on a field and a host snapshot on the wire, fire the s42 reload whatever the host's field is (not only when co-located). The guest is standing on its own field, so a same-field reload arms the mirror at a clean Main_Init.
- And/or force the COLD return (refuse the warm prime) for a boot whose guest is not yet mirroring, so the first mirror arm always lands on a Main_Init.
