I traced the path end to end in the live tree and it is reachable. No guard on the way looks at mirror state.

1. The host on the world map, or inside a field battle, publishes field 0, because its inScope is false off gMode 1. The guest's FollowHostTick returns at rs.Field <= 0 before the same-field branch, so SameFieldKickTick never runs. ServiceIntentFollow, the auto-teleport and the s144 world rejoin also leave a field-side guest alone (decision 5), so the mirror stays unarmed.

2. When the host draws an encounter, the guest's DioramaTick boots on purpose without a mirror gate. MayBoot passes through IsLiveFollowedSession, and the code even logs "the party mirror hasn't armed yet". The world-only gates (WorldBootWaits, WorldBootRefused) apply only when onWorld is true. Boot calls PrimeWarmReturn, and WarmVerdict has no mirror input. When the verdict is null, it copies ctx0 into ctx1 (inited 1, lastmap = the field).

3. On Leave, ForceDisarm, Disarm and Restore put the guest's OWN gEventGlobal back. Then the return's HonoluluFieldMain calls ApplyStoryBeforeEvents: BeforeFieldEvents keeps the copy, since ReturnIsOurs checks no mirror state. Next, ApplyStoryImpl's only gates are enabled, follow, role, connected and a snapshot present, and the host keeps publishing at 7 Hz from the world map. NetSyncState.ApplyStory overwrites section 0 unconditionally, and _storyMirroring becomes true.

4. StartEvents' reinit branch restores ctx1 and requests Main_Reinit. gEventGlobal is a separate array (EventState.gEventGlobal), not part of EventContext. So Main_Reinit and the restored own-story objects run under the host's flags. That is exactly the mid-field mirror-arm the s42 design rejected. The F3.2 design's DIO-1 suggestion, which became the warm return, assumed a guest that was already mirroring.

No GeoAttachOffset call in field 1405, so the offset is zero. Receiver: NetSyncClient.cs:1853 `DriveGhost(rs.Pos, rs.Rot, animId)` -> 9088 `t.localPosition = Vector3.Lerp(t.localPosition, targetPos, a)` under the fieldmap (8907). That is identical to localPosition for an unattached actor, whose parent is the fieldmap. For rotation, when pt.parent != ee.fieldmap.transform, send the last unattached rotation or the carrier's yaw: the world rotation under a (-1,-1,1)-scaled carrier is mirrored. findings.title: The bridge binds with SO_REUSEADDR on Windows, so a second bridge co-binds 49201 and the GUI's 'port in use' branch is dead for the common case
findings.claim: run_server sets SO_REUSEADDR unconditionally, and on Windows that lets two listeners bind the same 127.0.0.1:49201 with no error. findings.title: `coop --rebuild-room` with field 30003 registered in another active folder builds and registers a SECOND 30003 (cross-folder EventDB collision)
findings.claim: ensure_room skips its early return whenever rebuild=True, even when the room id is registered in a folder other than FF9Coop. It then builds FF9Coop with the same FieldScene 30003 and appends FF9Coop to FolderNames, which is the global-EventDB double registration its own docstring says black-screens.
findings.failure_scenario: On a dev install 30003 is registered by FF9CustomMap: the brief's id sample listed it there, and the band is the dev-scratch band agents mint from. The user runs `ff9mapkit coop host --rebuild-room`, whose help text reads 'rebuild the FF9Coop room even if a room is already registered'. find_registered_field returns 'FF9CustomMap', the `if existing and not rebuild` return is skipped, FF9Coop is built with FieldScene 30003 and registered. At the next launch two folders register 30003, one side loads the wrong .eb, and the co-op room (or the dev field) black-screens. Nothing here warns; deploy_field's own guard only warns and does not run on this path.
findings.evidence: coop.py:494-499: `existing = find_registered_field(...)`; `if existing and not rebuild: ... return existing`. :501-520 build into game/COOP_MOD and call ensure_folder_registered(game, COOP_MOD) unconditionally. :472-475 docstring: 'registering the same id twice black-screens'. cli.py:8703-8704 is the help text. reid.py:297-321 reserves COOP_FIELD for its own planner only.
findings.fix_sketch: When rebuild is set and existing is not COOP_MOD, refuse: 'field 30003 is registered by <folder>; rebuilding FF9Coop would register it twice -- remove it there first'. Or rebuild without registering. Also consider a check that refuses a co-op room id held by any other folder.

Neither the CLI nor the Workspace (jobs.py) has a guard. So a second 30003 registration is produced with no warning: the finding's mechanism is confirmed.

The consequence is overstated. Engine DataPatchers.Initialize reads each folder's DictionaryPatch in FolderLowToHigh order. AssetManager.cs:56-60 builds that order as the reverse of FolderNames, so FF9Coop (appended last, lowest priority) is read first and FF9CustomMap last. - Only the CLI can trigger it, behind an explicit opt-in flag. The Workspace Co-op tab never passes rebuild_room.

findings.title: FIFO lanes are not loss-proof through the bridge or relay (docs say 'latest-state, harmless'), and command frames carry no battle id, so a queued pick can land in the next battle
findings.claim: The bridge drops whole frames while its upstream redials, and the relay drops frames to a parked partner, on the stated basis that 'the wire is latest-state'. But types 2 (guest commands) and 6 (host actions) are FIFO lanes whose own contract is 'delivered exactly once as long as the link holds', and from the engine's view the loopback link holds throughout. Separately, the engine's out-queues survive a reconnect, and a type-2 frame has no battle nonce.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A guest commits a stock-menu pick during one of the bridge's frequent upstream redials. The bridge drops it, and 2.5 s later the guest hears the refusal buzzer and the menu reopens as if the HOST had refused ('REFUSED or lost'), with no way to tell. (b) On direct TCP, the link drops right after a pick is queued. EnqueueCommand keeps it across the drop (ClearRemote clears only the in-queues). If the outage outlasts the fight and the host's next random encounter has reached its command phase with that slot Ready when the link returns, the host's intake checks phase, ownership and readiness but not which battle. It executes the old battle's command id and target mask in the new fight. (c) The relay WriteLoop drains the FIFO queues into a batch before discovering the stream is dead, losing that batch.
findings.evidence: Bridge: `if state != "up": continue  # upstream down/redialing -> drop (newest wins)` (netsync_bridge.py:562-563). Docstring: 'The wire is latest-state at ~30Hz, so frames lost during the gap are harmless' (:23-25). Relay: `if partner == nil { continue // partner parked: drop the frame` (main.go:235-237), described as 'the wire is latest-state at ~30Hz, so lost frames self-heal' (:12-14). Engine contract: 'type 2 = battle command (variable; FIFO -- the underlying streams are reliable+ordered, so a queued frame is delivered exactly once as long as the link holds)' (NetSyncSocket.cs:81-82). ClearRemote clears only `_inCommands/_inActions/_inDialog` (:484-499); the out-queues persist. TryDecodeCommand is 9 bytes with no nonce (NetSyncBattle.cs:4875-4887). The intake checks HostCommandPhaseOpen, IsGuestOwnedSlot, and ReadyQueue/InputFinishList (:5912-5958), but not the battle. A lost pick surfaces as 'REFUSED or lost -- buzzer' (NetSyncBattle.StockMenu.cs:1445-1462). Relay WriteLoop: `while (_running) { due.Clear(); _frames.CollectOutgoing(due); for (...) WriteBinaryFrame(...)` with a silent catch (NetSyncRelay.cs:258-273).
findings.fix_sketch: Correct the three comments: FIFO lanes are best-effort across a bridge or relay gap, and the stock mirror's 2.5 s refuse path is the recovery. Engine: add the host's battle nonce to the type-2 frame (the control trailer already carries one since s114) and refuse a mismatch at intake. Clear or age out `_outCommands` on reconnect (drop picks older than ~2 s). Optionally have the guest mirror say 'lost' rather than 'refused' when PEER-ALIVE dipped during the wait.

findings.title: Bridge binds with SO_REUSEADDR, which on Windows lets a second bridge silently co-bind 127.0.0.1:49201 and defeats the Workspace's port-in-use error
findings.claim: run_server sets SO_REUSEADDR before bind. On Windows that option lets a later socket bind a port another listener already holds, and incoming connections are then split non-deterministically. The bind failure the Workspace relies on to report a busy port never happens.
findings.failure_scenario: A player leaves an old `ff9mapkit coop host` terminal running (bridge on 49201) and also clicks Start in the Workspace Co-op tab. The Workspace's start_bridge binds the same port without error and logs 'bridge listening'. The game's connections now land on either bridge at Windows' discretion; if one was started with a different --relay, --insecure or log file, sessions intermittently go to the wrong relay or log. Stopping one bridge leaves the other silently serving. The project already treats this as real in the harness (RECON.md:50 'Never 49201 (SO_REUSEADDR co-binds beside the owner's bridge)') but not in production.
findings.evidence: `server.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1); server.bind((listen_host, listen_port))` (netsync_bridge.py:777-779). The Workspace expects bind to fail: `try: self._server, self._thread = nb.run_server(...) except OSError as e: self._append_log(f"bridge failed to start on port {port}: {e}")` (workspace/coopdoc.py:535-540). The harness bench uses the correct Windows option: `if hasattr(socket, "SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE"): sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, 1)` (studies/test-harness/scenarios/_coop_peer_bench.py:488-494).
findings.fix_sketch: On Windows (`hasattr(socket, 'SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE')`) set SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR; keep SO_REUSEADDR on POSIX for TIME_WAIT rebinding. coopdoc's existing OSError branch then reports the busy port as designed.

votes.reason:
The finding holds, and I reproduced it on this machine rather than relying on documentation. Both ways of starting a bridge go through run_server, and run_server sets SO_REUSEADDR before bind (netsync_bridge.py:777-779). The only guard on the Workspace path is its own thread (coopdoc.py:529). Nothing probes the port first, and the setup subprocess runs with --no-bridge and checks no port either.

I wrote a scratch test on private ports 51877 and 51878 (never 49201), using Python 3.14.4 on Windows 11:
- A second bind of 127.0.0.1:PORT with SO_REUSEADDR succeeds, both in the same process and in a separate child process.
- As a control, when the first socket uses SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, the second bind fails with WinError 10013. So the except-OSError branch at coopdoc.py:537 is unreachable today, and it would work as designed with the proposed fix.

One correction to the claimed impact. Connections are not "split non-deterministically". In my measurement all 20 of 20 connections went to the FIRST bound listener. The harm is still real:
- In the stated scenario (an old `coop host` or `coop bridge` terminal is still running, then the player clicks Start in the Workspace), the Workspace logs "bridge listening on ws://127.0.0.1:49201" (coopdoc.py:541).
- Its poll then shows "connected through this app — keep it open" (coopdoc.py:457-463), because that label only checks its own accept thread.
- Meanwhile every game connection is served by the stale terminal bridge, with that bridge's --relay, --insecure and log file. The Workspace's in-tab log never shows the session.
- With the order reversed (Workspace first, then a terminal bridge), the terminal prints "bridge: running" (coop.py:631) and receives nothing.

When both bridges use the default relay, the game still works. That keeps this a UX and diagnostics issue, so low severity is right. The project already knows the hazard: the harness binds exclusively in coop_peer.py:1534-1546, duo.py:207-208 and _coop_peer_bench.py:491-4

findings.title: The ~ snapshot taint exemption checks the CURRENT role, so a co-op-tainted snapshot restores after a switch to Role=selftest, which has no save gate
findings.claim: RestoreSnapshot discards a tainted buffer only when `!IsMirroringStory && !IsSelfTestRole`. The selftest exemption is meant for bench-captured snapshots, but it reads the role at restore time, so a buffer captured as a real mirroring client restores the host's story once the role reads selftest. In selftest nothing blocks a manual save.
findings.failure_scenario: A guest (Role=client, mirroring) takes a ~ Flags snapshot, which is tainted. It edits Role=selftest; ApplyConfigChange arms the ramp, and the ramp reloads its own autosave. It presses Restore: _snapshotMirrored is true, IsMirroringStory is false, but IsSelfTestRole is true, so the restore proceeds and the host's gEventGlobal lands in the guest's live array. SaveLoadUI's gate (IsMirroringStory || Booted) is false, so a moogle save or Memoria's save hotkey writes the host's story into the guest's permanent slot. The autosave is also open when FollowHost=0 (selftest sets SuppressEncounters=_followHost).
findings.evidence: Ff9mkDebugMenu.cs:2880-2882: the taint is captured as IsMirroringStory || OwnSaveReloadInFlight || (IsSelfTestRole && BenchGates), without recording which; :2901-2910 is the discard test. NetSyncClient.cs:836-839 IsSelfTestRole = _enabled && _role == "selftest", read live; :1180-1186 a role change arms the ramp and :1397 clears _storyMirroring; :1650 selftest SuppressEncounters = _followHost; SaveLoadUI.cs:154.
findings.fix_sketch: Record at capture whether the snapshot was a bench capture (`_snapshotBench = IsSelfTestRole && BenchGates && !IsMirroringStory`) and exempt only those; any snapshot captured while IsMirroringStory || OwnSaveReloadInFlight is discarded post-session whatever the current role.

findings.title: Guest-driven co-op cells are saved into the HOST's permanent save and read as a phantom peer once co-op is off
findings.claim: Every role writes the peer's presence and position into gEventGlobal bytes 2032-2037 each frame. The mask exists only on the mirror apply, never on the save path, so a host that saves while paired persists presence=1 and the guest's coordinates. With [Netsync] Enabled=0 the client is never created, so nothing rewrites them, and kit [[coop]] gates on that save see a partner who is not there.
findings.failure_scenario: The host saves at a moogle while the guest stands on the same field, so gEventGlobal[2032]=1 goes into the slot. Later the host plays solo with co-op disabled and loads the slot. NetSyncClient.Ensure returns at once (no instance), so WriteCoopCells never runs, and a kit field's [[coop]] two-player plate or door reads CoopPeerPresence=1 and the stale X/Z, staying held or open.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:1229-1243 WriteCoopCells pokes g[2032..2037]; :1825-1829 the host also writes `WriteCoopCells(1, rs.Pos)` from the guest's position frame; :1891-1894 clears only while running; :680-683 Ensure creates nothing while disabled. NetSyncState.cs:22-24 and :120-125 mask only the APPLY. flags.py:224-227 says 'Save values are transient echoes (rewritten while co-op runs; never written when disabled)', so the saved echo stands forever when disabled.
findings.fix_sketch: Zero bytes 2032-2039 in the gEventGlobal copy that JsonParser serializes (the save path), or zero them at every field load when `_instance == null || !_enabled` from the static ApplyStoryBeforeEvents seam, which runs on every install.

votes.reason: The leak is reachable end to end. The default TargetField is 0, so co-op is active on every field. A host standing on the same field as its guest writes presence=1 plus the guest's X/Z into gEventGlobal 2032-2037 on every Update frame. That keeps happening while the moogle save UI is open: gMode stays 1, fieldmap and GetControlChar stay valid, and the guest's frames still carry the same field id. The SaveLoadUI save guard refuses only a mirroring guest or a booted diorama, so a host's save goes through. JsonParser then base64-encodes the whole gEventGlobal array, unmasked, and loading restores it the same way. The NetSyncState mask covers only the mirror snapshot/apply. With Enabled=0 after a relaunch, Ensure creates no instance, Update never runs, and the static ApplyStoryBeforeEvents seam does nothing to the cells when _instance is null. Nothing else writes to CoopCellBase. The live disable edge does clear the cells (ApplyConfigChange:1166), but that does not help a save made while paired and loaded in a later session, or on a stock engine. That also breaks content/coop.py's 'on a stock engine the presence byte is never 1 ... fail-safe vanilla' claim, and flags.py:225's 'transient echoes'. A second path with co-op still enabled: a relay client with no session code returns at :1727-1731 every frame before any cell write, so loaded stale cells survive there too. One correction to the consequence: a compiled [[coop]] gate tests presence==1 AND the peer's X/Z inside a plate rect (content/coop.py:111-128). Presence=1 alone opens nothing; a gate fires or holds only when the stale guest coordinates, which are field-local and come from the save field, fall inside a plate or zone on the field being played. That is most likely when the save point sits on the co-op field itself. If they do, a once-gate latches its flag permanently solo, and a hold-door stays open. [[coop]] is a documented, shipped kit feature (FORMAT.md/FEATURES.md), but the only in-repo user is the studies/
votes.mitigated_by: Partly limited by the gate design: content/coop.py:111-128 also needs the stale peer X/Z to fall inside a plate rect on the field being played, so presence=1 alone opens nothing. ApplyConfigChange:1166 clears the cells on a live enabled-to-disabled flip in the same session, but not on a relaunch or on a save loaded later.

findings.title: FollowHost is not role-gated in the engine, so a host with FollowHost=1 follows its guest and silently loses its own autosaves and encounters
findings.claim: FollowHostTick, StartFollowWarp and the encounter/autosave suppression all key on _followHost with no role check. The one playthrough that matters (the host's) gets no field-entry autosaves and no random encounters, and is dragged to the guest's field, whenever its ini says FollowHost=1. Only the Python writer prevents that state, so it is a law in a docstring for anyone who hand-edits Memoria.ini.
findings.failure_scenario: A user copies the guest's [Netsync] block to the host machine and flips Role=host but leaves FollowHost=1, a plausible hand edit that the b20 smoke test itself produced. On the host, suppress becomes _followHost && connected, which is true, so EventEngine skips every autosave (the host's Continue slot freezes) and random battles stop. FollowHostTick also warps the host back to the guest's lagging field, which is the two-field ping-pong coop.py documents.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:3689-3691 `if (!_followHost || _followWarpPending >= 0) return;` has no role test, and it leads to StartFollowWarp at 3744; :1802 suppress has no role test; EventEngine.cs:693 then blocks the host's autosave. coop.py:172-176: 'The engine's follow tick has no role check, so this is the one place both the CLI and the Workspace pass through: the b20 smoke test had a host ticked to follow'; coop.py:703-707 forces 0 for hosts. Compare SameFieldKickTick at 5022, which does check `_role != "client"`.
findings.fix_sketch: Gate FollowHostTick, ServiceIntentFollow and the suppress term on `_role == "client"` (and log once when a host's ini has FollowHost=1). The acceptance reasoning (that tool-side enforcement is enough) does not cover hand edits, and the host's save is at stake.

votes.reason: I traced the path end to end in the live tree, and the b20 smoke test already saw it happen in-game. LoadConfig reads FollowHost with no role check (NetSyncClient.cs:1003) and assigns `_followHost` unconditionally (:1105). In Update, a role=host machine skips the selftest branch (:1499 is for non-host/non-client only), creates its transport (:1719-1739), and broadcasts its own field. Both roles do that (:1750), so the host's `rs.Field` is the guest's field. findings.title: Teleport-to-host snaps onto any triangle at the host's XZ (GetTriIdxAtPos ignores the active-triangle flag), including ones the guest's copy has disabled
findings.claim: SnapToHost and SnapToHostAuto call SetPosition(target, true, true), whose triangle lookup scans every walkmesh triangle by XZ containment and nearest centre-Y without testing `triFlags & 1`. A snap can therefore bind the guest to a floor or triangle that is inactive on its own copy.
findings.failure_scenario: The host pulls a lever that activates a bridge or an alternate floor (a MAP-scoped walkmesh toggle the guest's copy never ran) and walks onto it. The guest presses F11, or auto-teleport fires. SetPosition finds the bridge triangle (inactive on the guest) and reports success, so the guest stands on a floor its walkmesh considers disabled. Movement off it may be blocked or erratic, or the guest walks over a gap the script never opened. A sloped host triangle overlapping a flat inactive one can likewise pick the inactive floor by centre-Y.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:8561-8567 SnapToHost and :8578-8588 SnapToHostAuto use pc.SetPosition(target, true, true). FieldMapActorController.cs:44-58 SetPosition goes through GetTriIdxAtPos, and :1279-1306 GetTriIdxAtPos takes the PointInsideTriangleTestXZ hit with the nearest |pos.y - originalCenter.y| and never reads triFlags. Contrast :1329-1348 GetActiveTriIdxAtPos, which filters `(walkMeshTriangle.triFlags & 1) != 0`. DESIGN.md:150-153 relies on GetTriIdxAtPos for multi-floor correctness.
findings.fix_sketch: Before SetPosition, resolve the target with an active-only lookup (GetActiveTriIdxAtPos, or a nearest-Y variant restricted to triFlags&1). If no active triangle contains the host's XZ, decline with a spoken reason (manual) or stay put (auto) instead of binding an inactive triangle.

votes.reason:
The mechanism holds in the live tree and real inputs can reach it, but what happens to the guest afterwards is milder than the finding claims.

Path traced: F11 or held L3 calls TeleportToHostImpl. It checks only:
- no warp in flight,
- not on the world map,
- the GUEST's own GetUserControl,
- a controlled actor exists,
- IsLiveFollowedSession,
- rs.Valid,
- same field.

None of these checks the host's scene, and nothing checks the walkmesh. The call then goes to SnapToHost, then SetPosition(rs.Pos, true, true), then GetTriIdxAtPos. GetTriIdxAtPos takes any XZ-containing triangle with the nearest centre-Y and never reads triFlags. SetPosition binds activeTri/activeFloor to that triangle, sets lastPos, and returns true, so the "snapped to the host" success line is printed. SnapToHostAuto also returns true, so its restore of `before` never runs.

How the two copies can diverge: in-field walkmesh toggles (BGIACTIVEF/BGIACTIVET, i.e. EnablePath/EnablePathTriangle, both MAP-transient) are never mirrored. Netsync has zero references to triFlags, triSetActive or BGIACTIVE. The guest's copy runs a toggle only when:
- the talk relay replays a host start (NPC/object talks), or
- a quad start whose window opens before the player moves (ladders and jumps are explicitly not replayed), or
- the guest itself walks into a tread region.

A host-only tread scene therefore leaves the copies different. Stock example: Alley 105. Main_Init runs EnablePath(2,0). Tread trigger e12 drives the Puck scene, which runs EnablePath(2,1) (e3 ip1113/ip1448), and floor 2 then stays enabled. If the guest did not walk into e12 and the host stands on floor 2, F11 binds the guest to a triangle that is inactive on its own copy. A second route: the guest keeps control during host scenes (the L1 pin is deleted), so F11 can also snap to wherever a host script has placed the host.

Where the finding overreaches: "the guest walks over a gap the script never opened" is refuted. Every frame, UpdateMovement runs

It only accepts active triangles and falls back to ResetPos, so the guest cannot walk across inactive triangles. It either drops onto an active triangle at the same XZ or stays pinned at the snap point until it steps onto an active triangle, presses F11 again, or follow-warps. Nothing in netsync guards the snap itself.

findings.title: Advanced() consumes a host CHO on a promise: the global VoicePlayer.closeDialogOnFinish, which any other window's Hide clears
findings.claim: For a voiced choice, ApplyEvents counts 'VoicePlayer.closeDialogOnFinish is set' as an advance and removes the host's CHO, but the real close depends on a VA callback that rechecks that single static. Any other window's page turn or close clears the static, so the committed choice never closes, and the guest cannot press again because its input is suppressed.
findings.failure_scenario: The guest has voice acting on. A host CHO commits a voiced choice W1: HostConfirm sets closeDialogOnFinish = true and destroys the other options, Advanced() returns true, the event is removed and ClosedByUs is set. Before the guest's option voice ends, a second window on the guest (a [TIME] caption, another speaker's line, or an ADV on another window) runs Hide(), which sets closeDialogOnFinish = false. AfterSoundFinished_Default then skips OnKeyConfirm(null), so W1 stays up for good. In stock the player just presses Confirm again. On the guest W1 is Locked (input swallowed), has no event, and the host has already closed it. It is released only when the host's whole scene ends plus the orphan grace, and the guest's script stays blocked all that time, so later host events age out (the first finding's consequences).
findings.evidence: Advanced :1287-1292: `|| (choice && VoicePlayer.closeDialogOnFinish)`. On a true result: `_inbox.Remove(e)` at :1372 and `w.ClosedByUs = true` at :1373-1374. VoicePlayer.cs:19 holds the one static. It is set by Dialog.cs:781-791 and cleared by every window's Hide (Dialog.cs:626 page turn, :638 close) and by VoicePlayer.cs:225-229. Record the Dialog reference HostConfirm committed, and if it is still CompleteAnimation on a later tick with closeDialogOnFinish false and no voice playing (VoicePlayer.HasDialogVoice false), re-drive it with HostConfirm. Better still, make the commit flag per dialog rather than one static (an engine-side VoicePlayer change).

findings.title: Cross-language pairs are 'unsupported' only on paper: the JP Confirm/Cancel swap inverts relayed script keys silently
findings.claim: The host relays its script-key hit AFTER ETb's JP layout swap, and the guest ORs those bits into its own poll unchanged. In a JP/non-JP pair the host's Cancel is the guest script's Confirm, and the reverse. Nothing on the wire carries the language, so the mismatch is never detected or refused.
findings.failure_scenario: The host runs EN and the guest runs JP. Both machines' JP and EN scripts swap the bits the dialog advance listens for (ETb.cs:79 comment, e.g. JP IsButton(589824) vs EN 655360). At a polled choice the host backs out with Cancel. The KEY carries Cancel, and the guest's JP script reads Cancel as its 'confirm' bit and commits the option instead of backing out. Conversely, the host's Confirm KEY never overlaps the JP poll's mask, so it is never served; it holds the key lock until the 20 s TTL, and the guest's beat is masked meanwhile.
findings.evidence: EBin.cs:1104 and :1135 pass `ETb.KeyOn(CurrentSymbol == "JP")` (already swapped) into FilterScriptButtons. On the host, TapScriptKeyIfHost computes `hit = keys & readMask & HostOwnedKeys` (NetSyncClient.cs:5607) and ships CompactKeys(hit) (:5630, :5639). On the guest, `(keys & ~HostOwnedKeys) | TakeRelayedScriptKey(...)` (NetSyncField.cs:905) applies no layout transform. The swap is ETb.cs:79-88. The only Localization read anywhere in Netsync/ is NetSyncClient.cs:5613, and no handshake or section carries the language. F3.2-DESIGN.md:796 and owner decision 10 (:994) accept 'same language required -- document it in the README', which is a law written in a doc, not enforced at the call site.
findings.fix_sketch: The acceptance is fine, but enforce it cheaply. Add the host's language symbol as one additive byte in section 7 (as s144 added b6/b7) or in the hello, and show an overlay plus disable the key relay and lock on mismatch. Alternatively, canonicalize: un-swap the host's hit to physical bits before CompactKeys, and apply ProcessJapaneseLayout to the relayed bits in TakeKey when the guest is JP.

Each machine loads its own language's .eb, and the JP scripts really do use swapped Confirm/Cancel masks. The HW exports show it: in test2_1, us IsButton(655360)/131072 sit where jp has 589824/65536. test2_221's Moogle_Male_37 is a clean case. Its Kupo Nut shop runs `while(!IsButton(720896))` and then a back-out test, `if IsButton(65536)` in the us block but IsButton(131072) in the jp block. On the host, EBin passes the language-transformed keys into FilterScriptButtons. TapScriptKeyIfHost ANDs them with the host's own mask and ships the compacted bits, with no language tag. On the guest, (keys & ~HostOwnedKeys) | TakeKey(...) is applied with no transform. TakeKey serves a KEY whenever its bits overlap the poll mask. Once a key is active, it returns the stored bits to any later read by that reader in the same tick, whatever that read's mask. Concrete outcome with an EN host and a JP guest: the host's talk start is relayed (section 6), so the guest runs the same handler on its JP .eb. The host presses Cancel. The KEY carries Cancel and is served to the guest's 720896 wait. In the same tick, the JP back-out test IsButton(131072) reads it: 0x20000 & 0x10000 = 0, so the guest does not back out (it runs RemoveGil/AddItem). The reverse also holds: a host Confirm makes the guest back out. For a plain advance (EN 655360 vs JP 589824), the Confirm KEY never overlaps 0x90000. While a KEY for the field is stored it holds the lock (KeyHold), masking the guest's own keys, until KeyTtlMs = 20 s expires or the idle purge clears it. Nothing enforces 'same language' at runtime. The only Localization read in Netsync/ is the held-tick check at NetSyncClient.cs:5613. The lock engages with no language gate. Owner decision 10 calls only for documentation, and the user-facing co-op tutorial (ff9mapkit/docs/tutorials/17-coop.md) does not mention language. Severity stays low: the configur
votes.mitigated_by: Only owner decision 10 (F3.2-DESIGN.md:994): same-language sessions are declared unsupported, and that is only written down in the docs. findings.evidence: HandleCommandPayload 6041-6062: the only item check is `ff9item.FF9Item_GetCount((RegularItem)id) <= 0`, then SendNetCommand(slot, cmdId, id, mask, cursor). The roster-side filter the host does not repeat is BattleHUD.Unity.cs:831-865 (HasItemEffect && ItemType.Item && use_condition). ff9item.2.cs:530-538: GetItemEffect falls back to `_FF9Item_Info[0]` with only a Log.Error. btl_cmd.cs:645-647 ItemUse. ActInstant 5962-5989 takes any `menu` via NetCommandForMenu (Unity.cs:672-680 accepts any BattleCommandMenu value). The mask and cursor are forwarded unchanged at 5997/6032/6055 into SetCommand, which writes `cmd.tar_id = tar_id; cmd.info.cursor = (Byte)cursor` (btl_cmd.cs:263-264).
findings.fix_sketch: At intake, re-apply the CollectNetMenus item predicate for ActItem. Restrict ActAbility/ActInstant to menus 2/3 (plus 0 for ActAttack). Validate the mask against the patched AA's TargetType: single types need exactly one bit, group types need the matching group. Derive the cursor from the mask bit count instead of trusting the wire byte.

votes.reason:
I traced the path end to end in the live tree and it is reachable. A paired guest that sends a crafted 9-byte type-2 frame while the host is asking for its slot gets past every intake guard. None of those guards checks the item's class, the target mask against the ability's TargetType, or the cursor. The engine's own inspection does not check them either, so the comment at NetSyncBattle.cs:5887-5889 ("the worst case is a no-op") is wrong for items and targets.

(1) ActItem with equipment works if the host has a spare unequipped piece in the bag, for example a Dagger. The only check is the count test at 6049. CheckCommandCondition re-checks the count only (btl_cmd.cs:1003-1005). GetItemEffect falls back to effect 0 with only a Log.Error (ff9item.2.cs:533-536). ItemUse then removes the item at SELECT_VFX (btl_cmd.cs:645-647 -> BattleHUD.Public.cs:846-848).

(2) Mask and cursor are confirmed. CheckTargetCondition (btl_cmd.cs:1238-1244) only intersects the mask with living, targetable units. The divided-damage and hit-rate penalty (IsDevided, BattleCommand.cs:127; BattleCalculator.cs:696-703) needs the wire cursor bit AND a Many-type ability. So a SingleEnemy ability, or a Many ability sent with cursor 0, given mask 0xF0 hits every living enemy at full strength. I did not trace each VFX's per-target ExecVfxCommand fan-out, but the targets are derived from tar_id.

(3) Correction: the ActInstant menu=4 case is usually a no-op. NetFirstAbilitySub returns 0 for an Item-type command because EnumerateAbilities yields nothing for Item (CharacterCommand.cs:17-27). That makes sub_no 0 = Hammer, and CheckCommandCondition then refuses it with NotEnoughItems unless the host actually owns a Hammer.

Severity stays low. Only a modified guest can do this: the honest digit panel and the stock-menu capture build frames from the filtered roster. The impact is cheating, or wasting the host's own equipment, inside a session the host chose to join, not a crash or a corrupted save.
votes.mitigated_by: Partly covered. The engine's CheckCommandCondition refuses item 0 (Hammer) when the host does not own one (btl_cmd.cs:1003-1010), so the ActInstant menu=4 scenario is usually a no-op. Nothing guards the equipment-as-item case or the mask/cursor case. The honest guest code paths never produce these frames (the digit panel and stock-menu capture build from the filtered CollectNetMenus roster), so this is reachable only by a tampered guest.

findings.title: The reconciler applies whatever battle the peer view holds, without checking it against BootedWireNonce
findings.claim: ReconcileTick drives the diorama's actors from NetSyncBattle.TryGetPeerUnits, which does no nonce filtering. A host that has moved on to a new battle has that battle's HP/alive/hidden/trance/ATB written onto the old diorama's units, while the action lane and the end block are both pinned to the booted nonce.
findings.failure_scenario: The host's fight 1 ends while its end is not presented on the guest (a cut over the end, or no end-kind block), and the host immediately starts fight 2 (consecutive scripted battles). On the first fight-2 sample, DioramaTick decides WatchWhyNewNonce and issues Leave. ReconcileTick runs right after it in the same Update and keeps running through the whole leave fade, because Active stays true until the scene unloads. It applies fight 2's units by slot: fight-1 enemies get fight-2 HP and hide bits, and a dead fight-1 enemy whose fight-2 slot is alive takes the revive lane (RemoveStatus Death, a corpse standing up), so the screen visibly scrambles while it fades out. In finding 1's FollowHost-off variant, no leave happens and fight 2 drives fight 1's actors indefinitely.
findings.evidence: ReconcileTick :3020-3046: `Int32 n = NetSyncBattle.TryGetPeerUnits(_wireUnits, out seq); ... ApplyUnits(b, _wireUnits, n, seq);`, with no nonce test. NetSyncBattle.cs:2651-2674 TryGetPeerUnits copies _peerView.Units whenever PeerBattleLive, whatever view.Nonce is. In contrast, the action lane pins frames to BootedWireNonce (the :200-208 docstring), and EndTick computes `ours = any && (e.Bench || e.Nonce == BootedWireNonce)` (:3887). The revive lane in ApplyUnit is at :3190-3204 (`btl_stat.RemoveStatus(unit, BattleStatusId.Death)`). The order in NetSyncClient.cs is :1946 DioramaTick, then :1955 ReconcileTick.
findings.fix_sketch: Have TryGetPeerUnits return the view's nonce, and in ReconcileTick skip when BootedWireNonce >= 0 && view.Nonce != BootedWireNonce (bench boots excluded), as EndTick's `ours` does. Also quiesce when LeaveRequestedRecently is true.

votes.reason:
The reconciler does no nonce filtering, and a real path reaches it. The path is a link cut that spans the host's fight 1 end and comes back while the host is in a later fight. Ordinary back-to-back battles do not need to be involved.

During the cut the guest's diorama sits in WatchHold, because the peer is silent. That hold can last up to SessionGraceMs, which defaults to 40 s. EndTick never sees fight 1's end block, so no end is injected and btl_phase stays PHASE_NORMAL.

When the link comes back, Pump adopts the new-nonce view (PeerAdoptStep returns AdoptNew for an unseen (seq, nonce)), which sets PeerBattleLive. ActionTick drops the fight-2 action frames, because they do not carry BootedWireNonce. DioramaTick sees a live lane with a new nonce, so DioramaWatchStep returns LeaveFinal/new_nonce and Leave() runs. Leave only requests Replace("FieldMap", FadeOutToBlack). It sets _leaveTick and mode, but it leaves _booted, _armed and btl_phase alone, and SettleForReturn returns early when no terminal end has been seen.

ReconcileTick then runs in the same Update. Its only guards are _booted, Active (which stays true while the scene name is still BattleMapDebug through the fade), PHASE_NORMAL, the load bits and n > 0. None of these test the nonce or LeaveRequestedRecently. So it applies fight 2's units to fight 1's actors by slot, and new 150 ms samples keep being applied through the whole fade.

ResolveWireUnit maps enemies by raw btl_data slot, so fight 2's HP/max, hide, trance and ATB land on fight 1's actors. KillUnit fires on slots that are alive in fight 1 but dead in fight 2. The revive lane (RemoveStatus Death) stands up a dead fight-1 enemy unless it has fully faded (die_seq >= 5 holds it dead), so the corpse stand-up is limited to recently killed enemies.

The nonce-pinned siblings confirm the inconsistency: ActionTick checks a.Nonce != BootedWireNonce, and EndTick computes `ours`.

The "no end-kind block, no cut" variant is mostly blocked in production. Guest
votes.mitigated_by: Partly covered. In the no-cut case, EndTick injects fight 1's end for every end kind (GuestMode is GuestOn in production), which moves the phase off PHASE_NORMAL and quiesces ReconcileTick; that closes the "no end-kind block" variant. The die_seq >= 5 check in ApplyUnit keeps fully faded enemies from reviving. Nothing covers the cut-resume-into-a-new-nonce path during the leave fade.

findings.title: The reconciler's design header still documents MISSING-AS-DEAD, which the code removed
findings.claim: The B3.4 reconciler header says an enemy absent from a wire frame is DEAD and that this is what makes late-join boots correct. ApplyUnits, 80 lines below, says the opposite: missing units HOLD LAST STATE, and the sweep was deliberately removed.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer (or a review agent) relies on the header and builds on missing-as-dead, for example by trimming DelCharacter'd units from the host's sample to save bytes or by reasoning about late joins. With no sweep in the code, a late-joining guest would keep enemies the host already destroyed standing until a sample carries them as Alive=false. Late-join correctness actually depends on the host sampling btl_data directly (dead units stay on the wire), a contract the header does not state.
findings.evidence: :2983-2986 '//   MISSING-AS-DEAD (enemies) -- a wire frame OMITS DelCharacter'd units, so an enemy the guest knows that is absent from the frame is DEAD on the host. This also makes LATE-JOIN boots correct ...' versus :3060-3065 '// A wire frame missing an index the guest knows = HOLD LAST STATE ... dead units stay on the wire as Alive=false ... (An earlier cut swept missing enemies as dead; the verify pass killed it ...)'.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the header bullet as 'MISSING = HOLD LAST STATE; late-join correctness rides on the host sampling btl_data directly (dead units stay on the wire as Alive=false)', and pin that host-side contract with a selftest row.

votes.reason: The comments do contradict each other, so the drift is real. But it is documentation only. The running code is already consistent with itself. The B3.4 header at NetSyncDiorama.cs:2983-2987 still says MISSING-AS-DEAD: an absent enemy is DEAD, and it claims this is what makes late-join boots correct. Fifty lines down, ApplyUnits (NetSyncDiorama.cs:3060-3068) does the opposite. It loops ApplyUnit over only the units present in the frame, with no sweep, and its own comment says the sweep was deliberately removed. The host sampler (NetSyncBattle.cs:2302-2313) walks btl_data[0..7] directly and keeps any slot whose btl_id == 1<<index. Stock DelCharacter (btl_sys.cs:314-328) only unlinks the unit from btl_list and cancels its running actions. It never clears btl_id, so a destroyed enemy stays on the wire with its Alive bit cleared: alive = cur.hp > 0 && no Death status, at NetSyncBattle.cs:2319 and 2340. The late-join correctness the header attributes to missing-as-dead really comes from this direct sampling. No runtime path today gives the wrong result. The failure needs a future maintainer to act on the stale header, for example by filtering unlinked or DelCharacter'd units out of the host sample. If that happened, nothing on the guest would ever kill those enemies, because ApplyUnits has no sweep, and a late-joining guest would keep them standing, exactly as the finding says. The finding slightly overstates one point: the header does not state the host contract, but the host sampler does, explicitly, at NetSyncBattle.cs:2304-2307 ('the dead as Alive=false ... no fragile missing-as-dead inference'). The study docs agree with the code: b34-recon.md:51 and diorama-lane.md:328 ('the missing-as-dead sweep REFUTED'). Low severity is correct. A related stale line at :2981-2982 explains the fully-faded case by the host's copy falling off EnumerateBattleUnits, but the sampler no longer uses EnumerateBattleUnits.
votes.mitigated_by: The running code is consistent: the host samples btl_data directly and DelCharacter leaves btl_id in place, so dead enemies arrive with Alive=false. The host-side comment at NetSyncBattle.cs:2302-2308 and the ApplyUnits comment at NetSyncDiorama.cs:3060-3065 both state the real contract, and diorama-lane.md:328 records that the sweep was refuted. The only exposure is a maintainer trusting the stale header at :2983-2987.

findings.title: World dioramas seat a party snapshot from the last FIELD load, never refreshed across world battles
findings.claim: A field diorama's warm return is itself a field load, so it re-parses the host's party sections (ParseSections) for the next battle. The world's warm return is not, so every world battle after the first seats NetSyncParty.Slots as they were when the guest last loaded a field: levels, equipment, support abilities, persistent statuses and KO all stale.
findings.failure_scenario: The host fights world battle 1 and a party member is KO'd; KO persists after a battle in FF9. The host also levels up and equips a new weapon from the world-map menu. In world battle 2 the guest's diorama seats that member alive, with the old level, equipment and status, all from the pre-walk-out field load. The reconciler's first type-1 sample then kills it on screen (a death at battle start), and the old weapon model and level stay wrong for the whole fight. Every further world battle drifts further, until the guest loads a field.
findings.evidence:
- MirrorHostParty seats from NetSyncParty.Slots[i] (2736), with status at 2828 and cur.hp/mp at 2836-2837.
- Slots refresh only through ParseSections at a field-load apply (NetSyncState.cs:100-101; NetSyncClient.cs:703-721, called from HonoluluFieldMain.cs:149).
- The world return seam BeforeWorldEvents (2347-2366) and NoteWorldReturn (2370-2406) do no party refresh.
- The reconciler corrects max/cur HP and death from the battle stream (3178-3208), so the visible stale effect is the start-of-battle death or revive and the unrepaired seat-only data.
- S145's known limit names only story writes ('takes none of the host's post-battle story writes'), not the diorama's party seat.
findings.fix_sketch: At a world wire boot, refresh a diorama-scoped copy of the party slots from the live state frame (the same pure read R8 does for the talk relay, NetSyncClient.cs:6757), gated on IsMirroringStory. Or refresh NetSyncParty at BeforeWorldEvents when a world return is pending and the guest is mirroring.

votes.reason:
I traced this end to end in the live tree and the scenario can happen in ordinary play. NetSyncParty.Slots is written in only three places: ParseSections, Clear, and the bench. ParseSections has two production callers, and both are on a field: (a) ApplyStory, which runs on every field load through the HonoluluFieldMain hook, and (b) the R8 talk-relay accept, which needs onField and a co-located host. Nothing on the world-map path parses the host's party sections. ff9InitStateWorldMap calls only NetSyncDiorama.BeforeWorldEvents, and that function touches only the warm-copy and song state. The world diorama's return is Replace("WorldMap"), so it never passes through a field load. The world boot path (DioramaTick, then the WorldBootWaits and WorldBootRefused pre-verdicts, then BootFromWire, Boot's world verdict and Arm) never refreshes NetSyncParty either. Arm's SnapshotParty only saves the guest's own party references. MirrorActive stays true across the whole world visit, because only the exit ramp and OnDestroy clear it. So InitBattleScene, then MirrorHostParty, seats Slots[i] as they were at the guest's last field load. That covers the KO/status bits, equipment (weapon model), the SA set, level and trance. The S144/S145 flow is: the guest walks out and stays frozen on the world map until the host enters a field, with no guest field load in between. Back-to-back world encounters in that window are normal play.

The client's own comment at the boot gate assumes the field case, where the mirror has "just armed" so the diorama "seats the RIGHT party". The world boot breaks that assumption.

What the reconciler does not cover: it fixes HP/MP, their maxima, Death, Trance and ATB at the first sample in PHASE_NORMAL. So a KO'd host member is seated alive during the intro and then dies on screen (or a revived one stands back up). Equipment (the weapon model), the SA-driven auto-statuses, and non-Death persistent statuses stay stale for the whole fight. Poison, Blind and Sile
votes.mitigated_by: Only partly mitigated. The battle-stream reconciler corrects HP/MP and their maxima, Death, Trance and ATB at the first PHASE_NORMAL sample (NetSyncDiorama.cs:3146-3252). The guest's menu content comes from the host's live roster (StockMenu.cs:431-435). The staleness ends at the guest's next field load (the s144 rejoin). The stale level is effectively invisible. What stays wrong: the KO/alive state until the first sample, equipment (the weapon model), SA auto-statuses, and non-Death persistent statuses such as Silence, which also feeds the mirrored-unit CannotUseMagic check.

findings.title: The frozen guest's world overlay says 'Rejoining' when no rejoin can arm, and gives no way out when the host is on a field this install lacks
findings.claim: WorldGuestOverlay never reads the arm's refusal. With the host on any registered field it shows OvlRejoining 'Rejoining your partner at field N...' even when WorldArmRefusal is refusing for a non-hold reason. When the host's field is unregistered, OvlPeerNoField's field wording gives a frozen world guest no escape: F11 declines, and the only release is a ~ debug-menu row.
findings.failure_scenario:
Case 1: the host enters a Dream World custom field the guest's install lacks. The frozen guest reads 'your friend is on field 30300, which this install doesn't have' with no movement and no hint. F11 logs 'not on this install', and it stays frozen for as long as the host plays there, unless it happens to find '~ > Co-op: release world freeze'.
Case 2: the guest sits on an event world, or has control off, or there is no fresh snapshot. The line says 'Rejoining ...' while the arm refuses every frame and nothing happens.
findings.evidence:
- WorldGuestOverlay (4706-4722): `if (hostField > 0 ...) { if (!hostRegistered) return OvlPeerNoField; return holdField >= 0 && hostField == holdField ? OvlWorldHold : OvlRejoining; }`. It takes no refusal input.
- WorldArmRefusal (3827-3853) can refuse on the event world, control, full map, snapshot, fade or latch.
- The OvlPeerNoField text (8782-8784) is field wording.
- TeleportToHostWorld declines on unregistered (8533-8537).
- The release is rendered only on the ~ menu World tab (Ff9mkDebugMenu.cs:1477-1485).
- Decision 8 accepts the release as the escape, but nothing on screen points to it.
findings.fix_sketch: Feed _worldRejoinWhy, a non-hold refusal, into the world chain as its own 'waiting: <why>' state. Give the world variant of OvlPeerNoField a second line naming the escape (~ menu > Co-op: release world freeze), or have F11 on the world map offer the release when the host's field is unregistered.

votes.reason:
I confirmed Case 1 end to end. Case 2 is mostly overstated.

CASE 1 (reachable): A following guest on the world map is frozen. In Update, onWorld is true, local is null and the session is not in grace, so the else-branch hits `onWorld && WaitLineOn` and calls SetWorldGuestOverlay. That function computes `registered` with the same eventIDToFBGID check. When the host's field is unregistered, WorldGuestOverlay returns OvlPeerNoField. Its text is field wording ("your friend is on field N, which this install doesn't have / a custom field needs its mod on BOTH machines") and names no escape. F11 / held L3 reaches TeleportToHostWorld, which declines through TpDecline. TpDecline only writes Memoria.log, so nothing appears on screen. FollowHostTick keeps re-firing WorldFollowFire, which refuses every frame for "not on this install". The freeze rule (SpectatorField = IsLiveFollowedSession) does not consider the host's field, so the guest stays frozen for as long as the peer is alive and the host stays on that field. The in-game release row exists, but it is drawn only on the ~ menu World tab, and no overlay line, the tutorial (17-coop.md:64) or any user doc points to it.

Two overstatements in the finding:
- The ~ row is not the only escape. The host moving to a registered field or the world map ends it, and so do unfollowing through an ini hot-reload (the Workspace/CLI stop), peer loss past the grace, and the exit ramp. None of these is in the frozen guest's hands on screen, though.
- On a pure-stock pair of installs every field 10-3100 is registered, so Case 1 needs a mod mismatch: the host on a Dream World custom field the guest lacks, or a ~ warp. That makes it a misconfiguration path. The code expects it (it has its own overlay state), but it is outside the "stock experience" the user is focused on.

The same discoverability gap applies to OvlHostTitle ("Your partner is at the title screen."). The debug-menu comment at Ff9mkDebugMenu.cs:1470-1471 names the title as the r
votes.mitigated_by: Partially: the ~ menu World tab's 'Co-op: release world freeze' row (Ff9mkDebugMenu.cs:1477-1485) is a working escape (decision 8). Other exits are the host leaving the field, unfollow or stop from the Workspace/CLI, and peer loss past the grace. On stock-only installs Case 1 cannot happen, because every stock field is registered. Case 2 is covered by decision 7's ratified wording and by the event world's redirect, which does carry out the rejoin.

findings.title: The world rejoin and watcher allocate strings and walk the object list every frame while they wait
findings.claim: While the arm is refused (the 15 s hold, an unregistered field, the reinit bracket), WorldArmWhy reruns every gate each frame from two callers. It concatenates new refusal strings and a dedup key each time, calls WorldTransitionWhy (an object-list walk when the cheap terms clear), and ReadWorldDurable calls FindObjByUID(0) every Update.
findings.failure_scenario: A guest frozen on the world map with the host on an unregistered field, or inside the 15 s hold, runs FollowHostTick's WorldFollowFire and ServiceIntentFollow's deferred WorldFollowFire every frame. Each call builds strings such as "the source-field hold (your own exit from it, under " + 15 + " s ago)" and `dest + ": " + why`, so there are thousands of small GC allocations a minute for as long as the wait lasts. That is avoidable GC churn on the 20 FPS world tick.
findings.evidence:
- WorldArmWhy (4065-4094) builds `key = dest + ": " + why` every call.
- WorldArmRefusal returns freshly concatenated strings (3833, 3849, 3851).
- WorldLatchStep allocates (3977, 3979).
- Called from FollowHostTick each frame past the debounce (3726-3729) and from ServiceIntentFollow while the intent is deferred (5384-5386).
- WorldDeclineWhyNow then ReadWorldDurable run every transport Update on gMode 3 (1945, 3205-3247), including FindObjByUID.
findings.fix_sketch: Have WorldArmRefusal return an int code and build the string only when the code changes, using a constant table for the fixed texts. Cache the durable projection per world load and change of travel mode.

votes.reason:
The finding holds for the arm path, but it is low severity and its ReadWorldDurable half is overstated. A following guest on the world map runs FollowHostTick every Unity Update. That covers both scenarios: the host on a field this install lacks, and the host still on the field the guest just left, inside the 15 s hold. Once the 1.2 s debounce passes, every frame reaches WorldFollowFire, then WorldArmWhy, until the gate clears. No dedup latch stops it, because _followWarpedTo is only stamped by a successful arm.

Each refusal allocates every frame:
- WorldArmWhy builds `key = dest + ": " + why` unconditionally (an Int32 box plus a concat) before comparing it to _worldArmWhyLogged. The log line is deduplicated, but the allocation is not.
- On the hold path, WorldArmRefusal also concatenates its message every frame. `(WorldHoldMs/1000)` is an int, not a string constant, so the compiler does not fold it.
- On the latch path it concatenates "a world transition is in flight (" + latchWhy + ")".
- The unregistered and event-world refusals return literals, so they cost only the key.

WorldTransitionWhy() is the last argument to WorldArmRefusal. C# evaluates arguments eagerly, so it runs every frame even when an earlier gate already refused. Once its cheap terms clear, it walks the active object list (BattleReturnInFlight). The walk allocates nothing.

ServiceIntentFollow adds a second WorldFollowFire per frame only while an unseen intent nonce is deferred for a registered destination. An unregistered destination is declined once and marked seen.

Where the claim is overstated:
- ReadWorldDurable allocates nothing on the heap. WorldWarmIn is a struct (NetSyncDiorama.cs:1784) and WorldWarmLeverName returns literals.
- FindObjByUID(0) is a linked-list scan that stops at uid 0 (EventEngine.cs:1167-1174), and the main object is normally at the head. The code's own comment at 3201-3204 already calls this cheap.

The net cost is roughly 2-4 small string or box allocations per fra
votes.mitigated_by: Partly mitigated: the log line is deduplicated (4087-4090); WorldReinitCached caches GetIP per entry-0 script (3261-3274); WorldWarmIn is a struct, so ReadWorldDurable allocates nothing; the 15 s cap bounds the hold case. The per-frame key and refusal string allocations in WorldArmWhy and WorldArmRefusal are not mitigated.

findings.title: The peer's submesh mask comes from a cached renderer list that includes held props and is never refreshed, so the ghost hides or shows the wrong submeshes
findings.claim: LocalMeshMask builds bit i from owner.GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(), cached once per player GameObject. A prop attached under a bone at caching time lands at the low indices: bones precede the meshes in the hierarchy, which this codebase itself records. Every later bit is then shifted against the bare ghost's renderer order for the rest of the field, even after the prop is detached.
findings.failure_scenario: Fields 61, 63 and 64 (the disc-1 play): Zidane_Init attaches the Sword to Zidane before the first Update, so the cached list starts with the sword's renderer. Fossil Roo 1405-1407: Main_Reinit attaches the Gargan_Flower on every warm return, which also recreates the GameObject and so forces a recache. In these fields, any per-mesh visibility change on the player shows up on the peer's ghost on a neighbouring submesh. The same index law breaks on the FallbackGeo path: a peer model this install cannot load is worn as Zidane, but receives the foreign model's mask (1857-1858, dressModel == 0).
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:9050-9059 `if (_localRends == null || !ReferenceEquals(_localRendsOwner, owner)) { _localRends = owner.GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(); ... }` then `mask |= 1 << i` per index. ApplyGhostMask (9065-9071) maps bit i onto the ghost's own GetComponentsInChildren order, captured at spawn (8914). The hierarchy fact is the s141 author's own: NetSyncSelfDress.cs:1717-1719 "geoAttach parents a held prop under a boneNNN, and on 11 of the 13 rigs bone000 comes before the meshes -- that read would be the PROP's material". BodyRenderer was fixed for it; LocalMeshMask was not. Init attaches in the exports: test2_12.txt:475 / test2_14.txt:937 / test2_15.txt:1142 `// Sword ; Zidane` in Function Zidane_Init (fields 61/63/64), and test2_389.txt:368 `// Gargan_Flower ; Zidane` in Main_Reinit (1405). The engine keeps the prop-free list itself: FieldMapActor.cs:44 `meshRenderer = gObj.GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>()`, taken at AddFieldChar before any attach.
findings.fix_sketch: Build the mask from local.fieldMapActor.meshRenderer (the engine's own list, taken before any prop), or filter with `r.GetComponentInParent<FieldMapActor>() == own` as BodyRenderer does. On the FallbackGeo path, apply _ghostRestMask instead of rs.MeshVis.

votes.reason:
The mechanism is real and reachable, but two of the reviewer's examples are wrong.

The real part: LocalMeshMask builds its renderer list once per player GameObject, and the only key is the GameObject (NetSyncClient.cs:9050-9055). It runs every frame in every role (:1746-1752). The ghost's list comes from CreateModel, which has no prop (:8890, :8914, :8951). The peer's mask is applied by index whenever dressModel==0 or dressModel==rs.Model (:1857-1858). In the field, a prop is parented under the carrier's bone (DoEventCode.cs:1570-1592 -> geo.cs:111-131 -> FieldMapActor.cs:267). In fields 61/63/64, DefinePlayerCharacter and AttachObject(sword) run in the same Init with no yield between them (test2_12:473/475, test2_14:934/937, test2_15:1116/1142). So the first cache of the new player GameObject always includes the sword, and the bits really are shifted.

Correction 1: for plain Zidane the shift is invisible. Zidane's battle_model overlay comes BEFORE bone000 (fakegame.py:1023-1027, battlewire.py:7590-7592), so its disabled bit stays aligned. The sword, mesh0 and mesh1 are all enabled, so the ghost's mesh0 gets the sword's 1 and mesh1 gets mesh0's 1, which is the same picture. Those three fields have no per-mesh HideObject/ShowObject on Zidane. A whole-object hide disables every renderer under the GameObject, prop included (ProcessEvents.cs:550-557), so the mask becomes 0 and the shift does no harm.

Correction 2: the cache is never refreshed, and that actually PROTECTS props attached later. Fossil Roo's Main_Reinit runs Wait(2) before its conditional AttachObject (test2_389:335 then :367-368). The first-frame cache is therefore taken before the flower exists, and the flower never enters the list. The same holds for the runtime attaches in field 1800.

findings.title: Memoria DIALOG text patches read SpeakerModelId / SpeakerAnimationId off the dressed body, so a model-keyed patch renders Zidane's lines differently on the guest's screen
findings.claim: TextPatcher gives every `>DIALOG` patch the speaker's live po.model, po.anim and idle. Self-dress rewrites those to the rig's model and mapped ids, so on the guest a patch conditioned on SpeakerModelId == 98 (or on Zidane's anim ids) stops matching his lines, while the host still matches them.
findings.failure_scenario: Any installed Memoria mod with a TextPatch.txt `>DIALOG` rule keyed on SpeakerModelId (a speaker name tag or portrait mod, for example) tags Zidane's lines on the host but leaves the same lines untagged, or tagged as the rig's character, on a dressed guest. The two screens then show different dialogue text for one host-authoritative line. No mod on this install uses the parameter today, so the impact depends on what a player has installed.
findings.evidence: TextPatcher.cs:131-133 `expr.Parameters["SpeakerModelId"] = dialog.Po?.model ?? -1; ... ["SpeakerAnimationId"] = dialog.Po?.anim ?? -1; ... ["SpeakerIdleAnimationId"] = (dialog.Po as Actor)?.idle ?? -1;`. The dress rewrites them: NetSyncSelfDress.cs:784-787 (`po.netDressSrc = asked; ... po.model = rig.Model;`), AttachDress 1116-1121 (the slots stored as mapped ids), RunAnimation 1368 (`ExecAnim(actor, dressPlay)`). The source model survives in po.netDressSrc (PosObj.cs:258) and is already used as the genuine model by NetSyncBattle.cs:674.
findings.fix_sketch: In PatchDialogString, pass `po.netSelfDress != 0 ? po.netDressSrc : po.model` for SpeakerModelId (and the raw source anim for the anim parameters, or document them as body-relative). The guest then evaluates text patches exactly as the host does.

votes.reason: I traced the path end to end in the live tree and found no guard that blocks it. On a guest that self-dress has dressed, the speaker's live PosObj reaches TextPatcher with its model, anim and idle already rewritten to the rig's values. The host's own Zidane is never dressed, because AtSetModel's SetModelRule returns DressNone unless IsClientOrSelfTestRole. So a TextPatch `>DIALOG` rule whose Condition reads SpeakerModelId, SpeakerAnimationId or SpeakerIdleAnimationId evaluates differently on the two machines for the same line. Netsync never overrides dialog text: there is no Phrase, ChangePhrase or TextPatcher reference anywhere under Memoria/Netsync. The guest builds every line locally, and the host only drives advance and choice. The trigger is not exotic. The host must set GhostAs to `auto` or a name; it is the Workspace's "They appear as: Auto" option and the playstyle fixture uses "auto". The guest's SelfDress knob defaults to 1. A moogle dress also arms, because charId 0xFF passes the arm. One condition is outside the engine: an installed mod with a TextPatch.txt `>DIALOG` rule that reads one of these parameters. No TextPatch.txt exists under the game install, and the parameter appears nowhere in the Memoria tree except TextPatcher.cs. That makes the impact hypothetical on this machine, but the input is real: it is a supported, documented Memoria mod format. A caveat on the fix sketch: SpeakerModelId can be fixed cleanly with `netSelfDress != 0 ? netDressSrc : model`. The raw source anim and idle ids are not kept on the body; only netJumpSrc and netDressSrc are. So the anim parameters would need new fields or a documented body-relative meaning.
votes.mitigated_by: Nothing in the engine prevents it. In practice it is limited only because no installed mod uses these TextPatch parameters, and the host's GhostAs defaults to "" (no dress) unless the host picks Auto or a name.

findings.title: The wire loco byte classifies Zidane's walk and run by exact slot id, so a host-dressed 98 ghost glides in idle on every variant or alias walk
findings.claim: ClassifyLoco only recognises the five modal slot ids, so SWORD_WALK, COLD_WALK, POT_WALK, MBG_RUN, TKE_WALK, FRA_WALK and the alias ids 190 / 203 all send LocoOther. Yet s140 already ships a by-NAME loco-class table (NetSyncSelfDress.LocoClassOf) that maps every one of them to Walk or Run.
findings.failure_scenario: A guest the host dresses from a 98 wire: a SelfDress=0 guest (owner D1 Option A keeps dressing it), an s117 guest, or any guest-side skip. In fields 62-64 (SWORD_WALK), 307, 1464, 1554, 1606, 1607, 2513, 2802, 2928 and 2705, the host's dressed ghost of that guest slides around in its idle pose while the guest walks.
findings.evidence: NetSyncVisitor.cs:207-219 (`if (anim == rig.Idle) ... if (anim == rig.Walk) ... return LocoOther;`). The sender is NetSyncClient.cs:1751 `NetSyncVisitor.ClassifyLoco(local.model, local.anim)`. On the host, GhostAnim -> LocoAnim(rig, LocoOther) = rig.Idle (NetSyncVisitor.cs:222-235, 466-469; NetSyncClient.cs:1851). The name table already exists: NetSyncSelfDress.cs:143-167 (COLD_/FRA_/MBG_/POT_/SWORD_/TKE_ variants -> Walk/Run). Variant fields are listed in polish.json open_issues[0]. The by-id choice is deliberate (comment at NetSyncVisitor.cs:205-206: "still classifies as Other, exactly as on rows 0-8"), but parity is the only reason given, and since the byte's meaning does not change, a by-name sender is wire-compatible.
findings.fix_sketch: On the sender, when ClassifyLoco returns Other for a rig-0 body, fall back to NetSyncSelfDress.LocoClassOfId(anim) for classes 1-5. Same v14 byte, no wire change; old receivers just get a better value.

votes.reason:
I traced the whole path from a real stock field. In fields 62, 63 and 64 the player entry is model 98 and gets SetWalkAnimation(3521) / SetRunAnimation(3508). These are SWORD_WALK / SWORD_RUN. The same pattern appears in 307 (2575 COLD_WALK), 1464 (7935 MBG_RUN), 1606 (4001 POT_WALK), 2802 (8555 TKE_WALK), and 2928 and 2705 (8847 FRA_WALK).

While the player moves, the engine sets actor.anim to that walk or run slot. The sender then calls ClassifyLoco(98, 3521). Rig 0 only matches 200/25/38/40/41, so the result is LocoOther.

On the host, GhostGuard keeps the dress, because the wire model is the plain-Zidane 98. GhostAnim then sees dress != wire and calls LocoAnim(dressRig, LocoOther), which returns rig.Idle. DriveGhost plays that idle clip on loop while lerping the ghost's position, so the ghost glides. No guard on this path re-classifies by name or checks SelfDress.

The trigger is reachable but needs a non-default setup. With the default SelfDress=1, an s140+ guest dresses itself, so its wire model equals the dress model. GhostAnim then plays the raw (already mapped) anim and the loco byte is never read. So the failure needs one of these:

- a pre-s140 (still v14) guest that never dresses itself.
- a guest whose body stayed 98 because of a dress skip or no arm yet.
