findings.title: The engine rewrites the whole Memoria.ini non-atomically, with no backup, to persist a minted session code
findings.claim: PersistSessionCode does File.ReadAllLines and then File.WriteAllLines (truncate and rewrite) of the user's entire Memoria.ini on the main thread with no backup. It then re-stamps _iniStamp, which also hides any external edit that landed between its read and its write. The kit's own writers do backup plus atomic replace.
findings.failure_scenario: A relay host whose ini has an empty SessionCode (hand config; the CLI always mints one) launches. LoadConfigIfChanged mints a code and rewrites Memoria.ini. A crash or kill mid-write, or a disk-full error, truncates the user's whole Memoria configuration (Mod FolderNames and every other section). If the Workspace writes a play-style change in the same window, that edit is overwritten, and the game's re-stamp at 1070 means the game never re-reads it either.
findings.evidence:
NetSyncClient.cs:1060-1071: `if (enabled && relayUrl.Length > 0 && code.Length == 0) { if (role == "host") { code = GenerateSessionCode(); PersistSessionCode(code); try { _iniStamp = File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(...) } ...`.
:1265-1307 PersistSessionCode does `ReadAllLines(IniFile.MemoriaIniPath)` and then `File.WriteAllLines(IniFile.MemoriaIniPath, outLines.ToArray())`, with no temp file and no backup.
Contrast coop.py:400-414 write_netsync: _backup_ini, then fsutil.atomic_write_text.
findings.fix_sketch: Write to Memoria.ini.tmp and File.Replace it with a .bak. Or better, never write from the engine: keep the minted code in memory, show it in the overlay and the log, and let the CLI or Workspace persist it. Re-stamp only if the file's mtime before the write still equals the stamp the game read.

votes.reason:
The mechanism is real and I traced it end to end. On a host with Enabled=1, Role=host, a non-empty RelayUrl and an empty SessionCode, LoadConfigIfChanged mints a code and PersistSessionCode does ReadAllLines then File.WriteAllLines. WriteAllLines truncates the file and rewrites it, with no temp file and no backup. The game then re-stamps _iniStamp from the post-write mtime.

The trigger is a real path, but a narrow one:
- The CLI host path always mints before writing, so the game never sees an empty code from it.
- The Workspace host path shells out to that same CLI setup.
- The harness pins fresh or parked codes.
- That leaves a hand config. The documented manual setup in tools/netsync-bridge/README.md tells the host to leave SessionCode empty.

Side defect: that README example, pasted verbatim, never reaches the mint. Memoria.IniFile does not strip inline comments after the '=', so `Role = host ; ...` parses as a non-"host" role and `SessionCode = ; leave empty...` parses as a non-empty code. The README's manual-setup block is itself broken.

The harmful outcomes are overstated:
1. Truncation needs a kill, crash or I/O error inside the roughly 1 ms WriteAllLines window. That window opens once per host setup (the minted code is then persisted), and the catch only logs.
2. The 'Workspace edit overwritten / never re-read' sub-claim needs an external write between line 959 (the parse) and line 1302, or between 1302 and the re-stamp at 1070. That is one synchronous main-thread call of about a millisecond, so in practice it is unreachable. The Workspace cannot produce the precondition itself, and its apply_playstyle needs a user click in that window.
3. Most importantly, stock Memoria already rewrites Memoria.ini the same way. Configuration.SaveValue -> ChangeValue/AppendValue use File.CreateText (truncate and rewrite) with no backup and no atomic replace. It fires on routine in-game config changes such as audio volume, battle speed and interface layout, far more often
votes.mitigated_by:
Three things already mitigate it.

1. The precondition is narrow. The CLI host setup (coop.py:677-688), the Workspace host path (coopdoc.py:500 via the CLI) and the harness (instance.py:319, duo.py:534) all write a non-empty SessionCode before the game reads it. Only a hand config with an empty code reaches the mint, and it fires once per host setup, because the code is then persisted.
2. The data-loss window is about 1 ms of synchronous I/O, and the concurrent-edit sub-claim is practically unreachable.
3. Stock Memoria's own Configuration.SaveValue (Configuration.Loading.cs:37-121) does the same non-atomic, unbacked File.CreateText rewrite of Memoria.ini on routine in-game settings changes. This adds no new risk class.

findings.title: 'Turn co-op off' or 'Apply now' during a running setup job is overwritten when the job finishes, and done() starts the bridge anyway
findings.claim: disable_coop and apply_playstyle write Memoria.ini directly from the GUI process and are not disabled while the 'Co-op setup' subprocess (room build plus write_netsync) is in flight. The subprocess re-reads and rewrites [Netsync] afterwards, and its done() callback unconditionally starts the bridge, so the user's last action is undone.
findings.failure_scenario: The first Start hosting takes about a minute for the room build. The user changes their mind and clicks 'Turn co-op off': stop_bridge has nothing to stop, and Enabled = 0 is written. The subprocess then reaches write_netsync (which re-reads the file at that moment) and writes Enabled = 1, Role = host. done(rc=0) runs refresh_status and start_bridge. The final state is co-op ON with the bridge listening, the opposite of what the user last asked for. An 'Apply now' made during the build is kept or lost depending on timing.
findings.evidence: coopdoc.py:518-525 starts the job through self._run, and nothing disables btn_off or btn_style while it runs (the only setEnabled calls are in refresh_status, :378-393). :564-575 disable_coop writes {"Enabled": "0"} immediately. :504-516: done() calls refresh_status and then `if not lan: self.start_bridge()` with no check for a user action since. coop.py:674-708: ensure_room (the long step) runs before write_netsync, which reads the file fresh at :409, so the job's write lands last.
findings.fix_sketch: Disable Turn-off and Apply while the setup job runs, or record a 'cancelled' flag in disable_coop and have done() skip start_bridge (and write Enabled=0 again) when it is set.

votes.reason:
I traced it end to end in the live tree and it is reachable as described.

1. Start hosting launches the setup through shell.run_job. That call is non-blocking: it starts an async QProcess and returns at once, so the Qt event loop keeps taking clicks.
2. Nothing disables the Co-op tab's controls while the job runs. _set_busy only toggles the console's Working label, the Stop button, the console button and the Deploy button. In coopdoc, the only setEnabled calls touch btn_start and host_box, and both are driven by install/engine state, not by the job. btn_off has no setEnabled call anywhere. btn_style lives inside host_box, which stays enabled whenever the engine is s37 or later.
3. A click on 'Turn co-op off' runs disable_coop. stop_bridge has nothing to stop yet, because the bridge only starts in done(). disable_coop then writes Enabled=0 straight away.
4. The subprocess (`coop host --no-bridge`) is still inside ensure_room. On a first host, that step does the real extract plus build_mod; coop.py's own comment calls it 'the minute-long room build'. Afterwards it reaches write_netsync, which re-reads the ini from disk at that moment and writes Enabled=1 and Role=host. That overwrites the user's Enabled=0.
5. The `--no-bridge` path returns 0. _proc_done calls on_finished(0), which is done(0). done() refreshes the status, which now reads 'ON, hosting'. It then copies the code to the clipboard and, since this is not LAN, calls start_bridge without checking for any user action since Start.

The final state is co-op ON with the bridge listening, the opposite of the user's last click. The Apply-now variant is real too:
- argv captures the play-style values at Start time.
- If Apply lands before the subprocess's write, the job overwrites it.
- refresh_status then calls _load_playstyle, which resets the widgets to the argv values, so the user's edit visibly reverts.
- If Apply lands after the job's write, it survives.

Mitigations that exist do not cover this:
- run_job's s

findings.title: `coop show` and the Workspace report a missing Role as 'host' while the engine runs the selftest mirror
findings.claim: The engine's default for an absent [Netsync] Role is 'selftest', but show_config defaults it to 'host' and the Workspace's refresh_status does the same. A hand-written 'Enabled = 1' block is therefore described as hosting while the game actually spawns a mirror ghost beside the player.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows an older note and sets just `[Netsync] Enabled = 1`. The game runs the selftest (a ghost walking at +250 x). `ff9mapkit coop show` prints 'role: host' with no selftest note, and the Workspace shows 'ON, hosting' with the Host radio selected. The user then debugs pairing on a session that is not hosting at all.
findings.evidence: coop.py:547: `role = key("Role", "host")`, and the selftest hint at :550 fires only for an explicit non-host/non-client value. coopdoc.py:399: `role = (coop.read_ini_key(ini, "Netsync", "Role") or "host")`, then :405 and :407 'ON, hosting'. Engine: NetSyncClient.cs:961 `ini.GetSetting("Netsync", "Role", "selftest")`, and :1114 `NetSyncBattle.SelfTest = _role != "host" && _role != "client"`.
findings.fix_sketch: Default Role to 'selftest' in both readers, which mirrors the engine, and say 'Role missing -> the engine runs the solo selftest mirror'.

votes.reason:
I traced the whole path and it holds. The engine reads Role with a default of "selftest", and that default applies only when the key is absent (IniFile.GetSetting). If Enabled=1, Update gets past the !_enabled return and takes the selftest branch, because the role is neither "host" nor "client". On any field (TargetField defaults to 0, which means everywhere) it spawns the mirror ghost at the player's position + (250,0). Memoria.log does show the truth ("config enabled=True role=selftest"), but neither kit reader says so.

The Python side gets it wrong. `coop show`'s key lambda turns both None (Role absent) and an empty value into the default "host". The selftest note only fires for an explicit value that is neither host nor client, so it prints "role: host" with no note. The Workspace CoopDoc.refresh_status runs from the constructor and the Refresh button. It also defaults Role to "host", so it checks the Host radio and shows "ON, hosting over the internet / on the home network".

The engine never writes Role back. PersistSessionCode writes only SessionCode, and no Memoria .ini template has a [Netsync] section, so a missing Role stays missing.

The trigger needs a hand edit. The kit's own writers always write Role: coop host/join write "host" or "client", and `coop off` keeps Role. So low severity is right. A bare "Role =" (empty value) mismatches the same way, since the engine reads "" and runs selftest.

Related trigger, more reachable and of the same kind: tools/netsync-bridge/README.md:46 documents `Role = host ; the OTHER player sets Role = client`. The engine's IniFile.Init keeps the text after '=' including the inline comment, so the role string is not "host" and the engine runs the selftest. read_ini_key strips inline ';' and '#' comments, so both kit readers report "host". The same README's `SessionCode = ; leave empty...` makes the engine read the comment as a non-empty code. That is a separate issue, out of scope here.

The proposed fix is right: default
votes.mitigated_by: Partial: the kit's own writers always write Role (coop.py:692), so only a hand-edited ini (missing or empty Role) triggers this. The engine also logs the real role to Memoria.log (NetSyncClient.cs:1125), and the mirror ghost appears visibly beside the player. Neither kit reader is guarded.

findings.title: The ghost skips stock's per-actor depth gate and per-field render-queue fixes, so it draws where stock would hide or re-order a character
findings.claim: Stock hides every renderer of an actor whose projected PSX depth falls outside [100, 3996] (frontCamera false -> SetRenderer). EnsureGhost force-enables every renderer, gives skinned meshes huge bounds and is never depth-gated, so a peer standing outside the local camera's depth range still draws. Field fixes such as 2924's renderQueue 2000 for Zidane never reach the ghost either.
findings.failure_scenario: In a multi-camera field, the peer stands in another camera zone that lies behind or very close to the local camera. Stock would hide any actor there; the ghost is projected through the local camera anyway, so it can appear as an inverted or oversized body on screen. On Crystal World 2924, a ghost of Zidane draws in the default queue instead of the 2000 that stock forces for Zidane there.
findings.evidence: Stock gate: FieldMapActor.cs:127-153 (`if (psxDepth < 100f || psxDepth > 3996f) { ... this.actor.frontCamera = false; ... return; }`) -> EventEngine.ProcessEvents.cs:529-557 (`!frontCamera` -> every Renderer under posObj.go disabled). Ghost: NetSyncClient.cs:8929-8938 (`renderer.enabled = true; smr.localBounds = new Bounds(Vector3.zero, new Vector3(100000f, ...))`), then only ApplyGhostMask with the peer's own mask (9065-9071); the ghost has no FieldMapActor (8855-8858). Field fix it misses: FieldMap.cs:615-618 `if (fldMapNo == 2924 && sid == 8) fieldMapActor.SetRenderQueue(2000)`.
findings.fix_sketch: In DriveGhost, compute psxDepth for the ghost with the same PSX.CalculateGTE_RTPTZ call FieldMapActor uses and hide all ghost renderers outside [100, 3996], or simply mirror the local field's frontCamera rule. Copy the per-field render-queue fixes (2924) onto the ghost by model and field.

votes.reason:
The code-level parity gap is real. The ghost is never depth-gated: nothing in Memoria/Netsync references frontCamera, CalculateGTE or the camera index. It also never gets the 2924 render-queue fix. But the failure scenario as written does not hold up when traced end to end.

(1) The "inverted body" for a peer behind the local camera is refuted by stock's own shader. The ghost wears PSX/FieldMapActor (NetSyncClient.cs:8941). Its vertex program sets oT1.z = -1 when camera-space z < 0 (FieldMapActor.txt:49 `slt r2.z, r2.x, c17.x`, :53-54). The fragment program kills those pixels (`texkill r1` on t1.z, :85-88). So a body behind the camera is discarded with or without the C# gate.

(2) The "huge bounds" are not a divergence. Stock forces equally huge bounds on every actor (FieldMapActor.ForcedNonCullingMesh, FieldMapActor.cs:303-324, `Vector3.one * Single.MaxValue * 0.01f`).

(3) The only way a ghost could wrongly appear is the near band: 0 < z and z/4 + depthOffset < 100. That needs a field with depthOffset < 100. Real .bgx data does have them (e.g. -282, -119, -1239, -2929 in extracted bgx files). It also needs a walkable point in another camera zone that sits in that band and still projects inside the local viewport. And the GPU must not clip it: shader depth = psxDepth (FieldMapActor.txt:51-52, oPos.z via VP at :59), and the field camera's near and far planes live in the scene asset, not in code. The reviewer names no such field, and I cannot decide it statically. The far band (>3996) draws a tiny ghost that is likely clipped or hidden by the background, which is also undecidable here.

(4) The 2924 claim is literally true and reachable if both players stand on Crystal World 2924. Stock sets sid 8's materials to queue 2000 (FieldMap.cs:615-616). The ghost keeps the shader's Transparent-1 queue, because EnsureGhost never sets a queue. But the visible consequence is unstated and unknown, and it affects one end-game field.

The cleanest real case of stock hiding a playe

Stock gives every actor the same huge non-culling bounds (FieldMapActor.cs:316), so the bounds change nothing. The ghost only exists when rs.Field == fld (NetSyncClient.cs:1825). findings.title: Sender never enforces MaxPayload, and an oversized frame is reported as a wire-version mismatch (endless reconnect on TCP, a silently stale lane on the relay)
findings.claim: BuildFrame encodes any length into the u16 header with no cap, while the receiver rejects len > 8192 through the same TryParseHeader that tests the version byte. A host whose state frame outgrows 8192 B is diagnosed as 'peer speaks a different wire version'. On TCP it disconnects, and because the oversized frame sits in the re-sent latest slot it does so again every 2 s for the whole session; on the relay the state lane just goes silently stale.
findings.failure_scenario: A heavily modded install (kit-minted [[item]] ids give the bag more than about 1000 distinct entries, plus many SAs and key items) pushes the type-5 frame past 8192 B. Direct LAN: every guest connection reads the header, fails, logs 'different wire version -- disconnecting', and reconnects 2 s later, indefinitely, while both players update engines that already match. Relay: the frame is dropped, the guest's ApplyStoryImpl logs 'no host snapshot on the wire (yet)' at every load, and the story mirror never arms.
findings.evidence: BuildFrame: `frame[3] = (Byte)(len & 0xFF); frame[4] = (Byte)((len >> 8) & 0xFF);` with no MaxPayload test (NetSyncSocket.cs:166-178). Receiver: `if (... buf[1] != Version) return false; ... return len >= 0 && len <= MaxPayload;` (:181-190), and ReadLoop maps any false to `_breakReason = "wire-version mismatch (update both machines' engine)"` (:678-685). Relay: the same check gates Accept with no log (NetSyncRelay.cs:356-357). Growth: AppendSection only grows the frame (NetSyncState.cs:137-151), and the bag adds 4 B per distinct item with no cap (NetSyncParty.cs:180-190). The only size guard is a selftest row for the dress frame (NetSyncClient.cs:7828).
findings.fix_sketch: In the Set*/Send* builders, refuse (log once and keep the previous slot) any payload > MaxPayload, and size the bag/key sections to fit. Split TryParseHeader's verdict into BadMagic, BadVersion and BadLength so the log and overlay name the real cause. On BadLength, skip the frame and keep the link instead of disconnecting.

votes.reason:
The code does what the finding says. BuildFrame writes any length into the u16 header with no cap. TryParseHeader returns one false for a bad magic, a bad version or len>8192. ReadLoop treats every false as "wire-version mismatch" and disconnects. The state slot is re-sent every 33 ms write tick, and ClientLoop retries every 2 s. So an oversized type-5 frame on TCP would loop disconnect/reconnect, and on the relay it would be dropped silently.

The failure scenario cannot happen with real inputs, though. I bounded every section of the type-5 payload:
- story 2051 B
- party 1451 B at most (4 slots, a 48-byte name cap, and the full 64 stock SAs each)
- key items 517 B (ids 0-255; Folklore mints inside 80-254)
- bag 1025 B (at most 255 distinct ids)
- intent/event/talk/dress 25 B
- dialog section 424 B (OpenCap 4, RingCap 32)

The worst case is about 5.5 KB, well under 8192. The finding's trigger, "kit-minted [[item]] ids give the bag more than about 1000 distinct entries", does not exist: the kit's items.resolve rejects any id outside 0-255, and [[item]] patches stock rows rather than minting new ids. To overflow, a third-party Items.csv mod would have to add about 700 brand-new regular items, and the host would have to hold all of them at once (on top of the whole stock set), or carry about 170 or more SAs per character. That is not a stock or kit situation.

The roster lane (type 4) and the battle lane (type 1) also stay far below the cap. The finding is a real but latent hardening gap. A cheap fix would still help: cap at the sender, and split BadLength out of TryParseHeader so the log stops misnaming the cause. But it does not show up as a defect in the stock experience.
votes.mitigated_by: Content bounds, not a guard. Stock and kit content cap the type-5 payload at about 5.5 KB: item and key-item ids stay in 0-255 (items.resolve), names are capped at 48 B, and the dialog section is capped at OpenCap 4 / RingCap 32. Overflowing would take a third-party mod adding hundreds of new regular items, all held at once.

findings.title: The talk relay permanently declines (consumes the nonce) when the NPC object has not spawned yet on the guest's copy
findings.claim: ApplyTalkStart returns -1 (decline, nonce marked seen) when FindObjByUID finds nothing. Every other not-ready-yet state defers, so a guest whose copy creates the object a little later never opens that talk.
findings.failure_scenario: The host enters a field and talks within about 1 s to an NPC that the field script creates after an initial delay, or one that walks in on a timer. The guest's copy loads slightly behind, reaches FieldHUD with control on (the relay's preconditions), and runs ApplyTalkStart before its own InitObject for that uid. The talk is declined once ('no object with uid N on this field -- ignored') and _lastTalkNonce = nonce, so it is never retried inside the 4 s TTL. The guest never sees the conversation, the host's events age out, and the guest's copy of that NPC's MAP state (talked-to counters) diverges.
findings.evidence: ApplyTalkStart NetSyncClient.cs:6788-6796 returns -1 when obj == null. ServiceTalkFollow :6737-6747 consumes the nonce for anything but 0. The siblings defer instead: 'no controlled actor yet' :6798-6802, control off :6803-6807, the object still running :6808-6812. The section rides TalkRelayTtlMs (:5176-5177), so a defer is already bounded.
findings.fix_sketch: Treat a missing object as a DEFER (return 0 with deferWhy 'object not spawned yet') while the talk section is still on the lane. The host TTL already bounds it, and the expiry line at :6704-6707 logs the miss.

votes.reason:
The code reading is accurate. ApplyTalkStart returns -1 when FindObjByUID returns null (NetSyncClient.cs:6791-6796), and ServiceTalkFollow then consumes the nonce (:6746). The other not-ready states defer (:6797-6812).

The trigger the finding names cannot happen in stock FF9: a guest copy that creates the talked-to NPC "a little later" (a delayed InitObject, or an NPC that walks in on a timer).
(1) Every InitObject in the game lives in Main_Init. I counted the 817 HW exports in C:/gd/FFIX/reference/test2: 11,416 of 11,416 calls are inside Main_Init, none in any other function. A path-aware scan (scratchpad verify/scan_late_init4.py) found 0 SpeakBTN-bearing objects created after a real Main_Init yield, once the dev-only "Error Set Scenario Counter" guard is excluded. Only one object of any kind is created after a yield: PinnacleRocks_Stone in field 2500, which is not talkable.
(2) Main_Init's first segment runs synchronously inside the field's first-frame init. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:209 calls ff9InitStateFieldMap. That sets ee.fieldmap at :113, then calls StartEvents at :150, which runs ProcessEvents at EventEngine.cs:763, all in one call. Before :113, ee.fieldmap is the destroyed old-scene component, so the Unity null check makes onField false (NetSyncClient.cs:1429). No netsync tick can therefore see the new field before its talkable NPCs exist.
(3) A walk-in-on-a-timer NPC already exists from Main_Init, so FindObjByUID finds it. Its still-running or control-off states already defer at :6803-6812.

On a co-located FieldHUD tick, a missing uid means the guest's Main_Init took a different branch, for example an InitObject conditional on FieldEntrance or the party (test2_244 Dagger/Steiner). That object never appears, so declining now and deferring until the 4 s TTL expires end the same way. Only the log line differs.

Separate lead, not the reported mechanism, and not decidable statically: the field-shutdown frame. HonoluluFieldMain.cs:310 calls shutdownField, and :
votes.mitigated_by: Stock content creates every object in Main_Init's synchronous first segment, which runs inside StartEvents within ff9InitStateFieldMap, before onField can be true. A uid still missing after that is permanent (a branch divergence), so declining it gives the same result as deferring it to the TTL expiry.

findings.title: Guest-issued commands lose their command menu (cmdMenu None) and are validated with command/menu None, unlike the same pick made locally
findings.claim: SendNetCommand calls SetCommand without cmdMenu, so cmd.info.cmdMenu stays BattleCommandMenu.None. Its validator (GetAbilityState with an explicit playerIndex) also evaluates ability features and MP patches with command and menu None. Any Memoria/kit feature keyed on CommandMenu or CommandId therefore resolves differently for a guest's pick than for the identical local pick.
findings.failure_scenario: A Dream World IX custom ability or support ability uses an NCalc condition or MP patch on CommandMenu or CommandId (the [[playable]] effect/feature path). Picked by the guest, it is accepted or refused differently, or costs different MP in CheckMpCondition, than the same pick on the host. The host's battle diverges from what the guest's menu showed. Stock data does not key on CommandMenu, so vanilla content is unaffected.
findings.evidence: BattleHUD.Unity.cs:662 `btl_cmd.SetCommand(cmd, commandId, subNo, tarId, cursor);`, with no cmdMenu argument. Stock SendCommand at BattleHUD.cs:1764 passes `cmdMenu: command.Menu`. SetCommand btl_cmd.cs:175 `cmd.info.cmdMenu = cmdMenu;`. Consumers: CheckMpCondition btl_cmd.cs:1203 (GetPatchedMPCost(..., cmd.cmd_no, cmd.info.cmdMenu, ...)), BattleAbilityHelper.cs:90/95/148, and NCalcUtility.cs:656 `expr.Parameters["CommandMenu"] = (Int32)command.CommandMenu`. The validator path: NetAbilityUsable (Unity.cs:735) -> GetAbilityState(abilId, playerIndex) with checkCurrentPlayer=false -> BattleHUD.cs:1395 IsAbilityDisabled(..., None, None) and 1397 GetActionMpCost(..., considerCommandMenu false).
findings.fix_sketch: Thread the wire menu through: SendNetCommand(..., BattleCommandMenu menu) -> SetCommand(..., cmdMenu: menu), passing Attack/Defend/Item for those actions. Add command/menu parameters to the validator, so IsAbilityDisabled and GetPatchedMPCost see the same command and menu as a local pick.

votes.reason: The code facts are correct, but nothing real triggers the failure, and part of the impact claim is wrong. The facts: on the host, a guest pick goes HandleCommandPayload (ActAbility) -> NetAbilityUsable -> GetAbilityState(abilId, playerIndex), which evaluates with CommandId None and CommandMenu None (BattleHUD.cs:1395, 1397/1301). It is then queued by SendNetCommand -> SetCommand with no cmdMenu (Unity.cs:662), so cmd.info.cmdMenu stays None at CheckMpCondition (btl_cmd.cs:1203). The failure needs content whose ability features key on CommandMenu, or CommandId inside an AA Disable/MPCost feature. No such content exists anywhere I checked: (1) the stock install's AbilityFeatures.txt and FF9CustomMap's copy have 0 CommandMenu hits; every CommandId hit is a comment or an SA Cover/Protect Girls Command trigger on EnemyAtk. (2) No .txt/.csv in the whole install mentions CommandMenu. (3) The kit never emits CommandMenu: zero hits in ff9mapkit/ff9mapkit or any non-.cs repo file except co-op patches and harness scenarios. Its only emitted CommandId condition is the summon short/full roll (summons/deploy.py:1386), an SA 'Command' trigger evaluated against the real cmd.cmd_no. SetCommand sets cmd_no correctly for guest picks (btl_cmd.cs:164), so that roll is unaffected. The only way to reach it is a user hand-writing a raw [[ability_feature]] / effect string that reads CommandMenu. Two parts of the impact claim are wrong. (b) CommandId is correct at execution: ApplySpecialCommandCondition, CheckMpCondition and the SA triggers all read cmd.cmd_no, so the CommandId half only matters for validation. Stock Memoria alr
votes.mitigated_by: No shipped, installed or kit-emitted ability feature reads CommandMenu. CommandId is correct at execution (btl_cmd.cs:164). The guest's menu is the host roster, computed with the same None/None path as the validator (Unity.cs:812/819), so display and validation agree. findings.title: EnsureGhost's catch drops a half-built ghost GameObject without destroying it, and the caller retries every frame
findings.claim: Any exception after CreateModel returns g leaves g alive: parented under the fieldmap, a registered GeoTexAnim HonoBehavior, renderers possibly force-enabled. Only _ghost is nulled, so the next frame's EnsureGhost builds another one.
findings.failure_scenario: A throw inside the try after line 8890, while both players stay co-located, leaves an orphaned frozen body and a live HonoBehavior. Candidates: GeoTexAnim's CSV Int32.Parse, AddAnimToGameObject's animationEventClip[animName] KeyNotFound for a mod's EventAnimation list that names a clip missing from its line 0, or the material and normal steps for a modded or loose-FBX peer model. With a deterministic throw that becomes one per frame, at roughly 30-60 GameObjects, Animation components and HonoBehaviors a second.
findings.evidence: NetSyncClient.cs:8890 `GameObject g = ModelFactory.CreateModel(...)`; 8903-8945 (addTexAnim, AddAnimToGameObject, parent, layer, force-enable, material, shader and normal steps); 8961-8965 `catch (Exception err) { Log.Error(err, "[NetSync] ghost spawn failed"); _ghost = null; }` with g never destroyed. Retry: 1847 calls EnsureGhost every co-located frame, and the guard at 8866/8871 is `_ghost != null`. Throwing sites: AnimationFactory.AddAnimToGameObject `AnimationClip clip = AnimationFactory.animationEventClip[animName];` and GeoTexAnim.cs:259 `Int32.Parse(entry[0])`.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep g in a local. In the catch, if g != null, tear it down the sanctioned way (its GeoTexAnim's UnregisterHonoBehavior(dispose:true), else Object.Destroy), then latch a per-model failure (for example _ghostFailModel plus a cooldown) so a deterministic fault logs once instead of rebuilding each frame.

votes.reason:
The code shape the reviewer describes is accurate. In the catch, `g` is never torn down, only `_ghost` is set to null. Neither guard at 8866/8871 latches a failure, so line 1847 would rebuild the ghost on every co-located frame. But the failure scenario needs a throw after CreateModel returns `g`, and I could not trace any real input that causes one.

(1) The AddAnimToGameObject KeyNotFound at 8904 cannot happen there. ModelFactory.CreateModel already makes the identical call at ModelFactory.cs:171 with the same object and the same geo string (`modelNameId = path`, line 52). So a missing `animationEventClip[animName]` key would throw inside CreateModel, before `g` is assigned. On the second pass every clip that was added is skipped by `GetClip(animName) != null`, and neither dictionary changes in between.

(2) The GeoTexAnim CSV `Int32.Parse`, the shader, SetMatFilter and NormalSolver steps are the engine's own unguarded per-actor path, in the same order on the same geo. That path is SetModel (DoEventCode.cs:1108-1109), updateModelsToBeAdded.cs:25-26, CharacterBuilder.cs:84-89, then FieldMap.AddFieldChar 593-607. None of them has a try/catch. A model whose assets throw deterministically would already break every field that spawns it.

(3) The models the ghost can wear are a closed set, and every one is spawned through that same engine path. They are FallbackGeo Zidane, the GhostAs named and party models (the moogle is 220, plus cinna, marcus, blank and beatrix; NetSyncVisitor.cs:31,128,178), or `rs.Model`. `rs.Model` is the peer's control character, which the peer's engine built through SetModel. An unknown id falls back to Zidane (8888-8889), and a model that fails to load also falls back (8892-8897).

That leaves only two ways to reach a throw. One is a broken or divergent local asset for a peer model this install never spawns on its own fields. The other is the IsSelfTestRole `wire <model>` bench lever (1652). Neither is a real user path.

Even if a throw did hap
votes.mitigated_by: Engine parity: every step after CreateModel in EnsureGhost (addTexAnim, shader/filter, SmoothCharacterMesh) is the same unguarded per-actor path the engine runs for every field spawn of the same geo (DoEventCode SetModel, updateModelsToBeAdded, AddFieldChar). The AddAnimToGameObject call at 8904 repeats one CreateModel already made at ModelFactory.cs:171. The ghost's model set is closed (fallback Zidane, GhostAs names, the peer's field-spawned control character). Any orphan is removed at the next field load.
